Exam: T 99.9 F, oropharynx erythematous with patchy tonsillar exudates, no trismus, neck supple without adenopathy, lungs clear. Rapid strep negative; monospot not indicated at age. Impression: acute pharyngitis, likely viral. Plan: supportive care with fluids, acetaminophen, salt-water gargles, throat lozenges. Return precautions for inability to swallow, drooling, or worsening breathing. Primary care follow-up in 3-5 days if not improving.

34-year-old woman evaluated in urgent care. Four days of facial pressure over the maxillary region, purulent nasal discharge, congestion, and low-grade fever, consistent with acute bacterial sinusitis. She additionally reports a two-week history of midline low back pain and stiffness after lifting boxes, without radiation or neurologic deficits; exam shows lumbar paraspinal tenderness and limited flexion, negative straight leg raise, consistent with dorsalgia, musculoskeletal in nature. Plan: amoxicillin-clavulanate for 10 days, saline irrigation, ibuprofen and heat, gentle stretching; return if worsening pain or red flags.

ICU admission: 32-year-old female admitted with fever, tachycardia 128, hypotension requiring vasopressors, and confusion; blood cultures pending, lactate 4.2 — meeting criteria for sepsis, source being evaluated. She has a known history of thyrotoxicosis on methimazole, currently with suppressed TSH and tachyarrhythmias, endocrinology consulted for thyroid storm precautions. Left leg swelling and tenderness prompted duplex ultrasound showing proximal deep vein thrombosis; therapeutic heparin started. Labs also show hemoglobin 8.4, MCV 68, ferritin 5 — iron deficiency anemia, transfusion held for now, iron repletion planned after stabilization. Plan: broad-spectrum antibiotics, anticoagulation, beta-blockade, continue methimazole, serial hemodynamics and labs, and reassess anemia and hyperthyroidism once acute illness stabilizes.

Hospital admission: 40-year-old female presented to the ED with 24 hours of worsening right lower quadrant pain, anorexia, nausea; CT abdomen shows a dilated appendix with periappendiceal fat stranding — acute appendicitis; taken for laparoscopic appendectomy, doing well postoperatively. Preoperative labs revealed hemoglobin 8.2 with microcytic, hypochromic indices and low ferritin consistent with iron deficiency anemia, as well as a normocytic anemia component on smear felt to represent an additional unspecified anemia; hematology consulted. She also has right leg swelling; duplex ultrasound confirms a right femoral deep vein thrombosis, therapeutic enoxaparin started postoperatively with transition to apixaban. Iron supplementation begun; repeat CBC in 2 weeks; hematology and vascular follow-up arranged.

Telehealth endocrinology follow-up. 73-year-old female with thyrotoxicosis complains of palpitations, heat intolerance, tremor, and 8-lb weight loss despite good appetite. TSH suppressed at <0.01, free T4 elevated at 3.1. She has well-demarcated scaly erythematous plaques with silvery scale over the extensor elbows and knees, consistent with her chronic psoriasis; topical steroid cream renewed. Plan: continue methimazole 10 mg daily, add propranolol for symptom control, repeat thyroid panel in 6 weeks, deratology referral if psoriasis flares further.

ED note. 85-year-old female presents with three days of cough, sore throat, and nasal congestion consistent with acute upper respiratory infection, plus generalized myalgias and bilateral leg pain without swelling, erythema, or trauma. Labs notable for hemoglobin 9.8, MCV 72, ferritin low, consistent with iron deficiency anemia; no overt bleeding, stool occult blood negative. Exam: afebrile, pharynx mildly erythematous, chest clear, limbs tender to palpation diffusely but no joint swelling, pulses intact. Plan: supportive care for the viral URI, fluids and rest; oral ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily with vitamin C; repeat CBC in 6 weeks; soft tissue pain managed with acetaminophen; return if bleeding or worsening symptoms.

Telehealth visit. 51-year-old male presents for follow-up regarding tobacco use. Reports smoking one pack per day for the past 30 years, first cigarette within 10 minutes of waking each morning. Has attempted to quit twice in the past year, longest abstinence was three weeks. Fagerstrom score consistent with heavy dependence. No cough, no chest pain. Exam limited on video; patient appears well, no apparent distress. Plan: initiate varenicline taper pack, start 0.5 mg daily titrating to 1 mg twice daily. Behavioral counseling referral to quitline. Follow-up in four weeks to assess cravings and medication tolerance.

Nephrology clinic. 57-year-old female with chronic kidney disease followed here; today's labs show eGFR 38 mL/min/1.73m2, creatinine 1.7 mg/dL, stable from prior visits, urine albumin-to-creatinine ratio elevated; continues lisinopril and avoids NSAIDs. She reports persistent diffuse muscle aches and bone discomfort; 25-hydroxy vitamin D level measured at 12 ng/mL, consistent with vitamin D deficiency, likely contributing to her symptoms and secondary hyperparathyroidism risk in kidney disease. Exam unremarkable aside from mild proximal muscle tenderness. Plan: cholecalciferol 50,000 units weekly for eight weeks then maintenance dosing adjusted for renal function, repeat vitamin D and PTH levels, continue renal-protective therapy, and renal nutrition consult. Next visit with repeat BMP and eGFR in three months.

Clinic visit with caregiver present. 73-year-old female with Alzheimer disease, now moderate stage — worsening short-term memory, repeats questions, needs help with medications. Caregiver reports loud snoring with gasping at night and daytime napping; Epworth 12/24, sleep study confirmed obstructive sleep apnea — CPAP ordered. She also reports 5 days of facial pressure, purulent nasal discharge, and headache — acute sinusitis; started on amoxicillin-clavulanate and saline irrigation. Bilateral knee pain with crepitus on exam and joint-space tenderness, worse with stairs — osteoarthritis of both knees; continue acetaminophen, refer to physiotherapy, discuss intra-articular steroid injection if refractory. Repeat cognitive testing in 3 months.

23M admitted via ED with LLQ abdominal pain and fever. CT abdomen with contrast shows sigmoid diverticula with surrounding inflammatory stranding — diverticulitis of the sigmoid colon. Made NPO, started IV ceftriaxone and metronidazole, improving; advance diet as tolerated. Incidentally, patient has long-standing seropositive rheumatoid arthritis, diagnosed age 19, involving hands, wrists and knees with morning stiffness > 1 hour; currently on methotrexate 20 mg weekly and folic acid, holding biologic during acute infection. Rheumatology consulted to coordinate resumption of therapy after antibiotics complete. Plan: 10-day antibiotic course, outpatient GI follow-up for colonoscopy in 6-8 weeks, rheumatology clinic in 4 weeks.

Telehealth encounter. 28-year-old male veteran referred for nightmares, hypervigilance, avoidance of crowds, and flashbacks since returning from deployment two years ago. He describes startle response to loud noises, sleep disturbance, and irritability straining his relationship. He recently separated from service and is struggling to adjust to civilian work. PHQ-9 and PTSD checklist consistent with post-traumatic stress disorder. Plan: begin trauma-focused CBT weekly, started sertraline 50 mg daily titrating upward, sleep hygiene counseling, and referral to peer support group. Safety planning reviewed; no suicidal ideation endorsed. Follow-up in four weeks.

Clinic follow-up, 29-year-old female here for routine care of her type 1 diabetes mellitus. She uses multiple daily injections of lispro and glargine; A1c today 7.4%, CGM downloads show no severe hypoglycemia. She has also been noted to have elevated blood pressures over the last three visits, today 152/96, confirmed on repeat measurement; basic metabolic panel and urinalysis unremarkable, no end-organ findings on exam. Essential hypertension diagnosed. Plan: continue current insulin regimen, start lisinopril 10 mg daily, home BP log, recheck in four weeks, reinforce diet and exercise.

Clinic visit. 70-year-old female presents with 3 days of sore throat, nasal congestion, and dry cough, consistent with an acute upper respiratory infection. She has long-standing seropositive erosive rheumatoid arthritis affecting the small joints of both hands, currently managed with methotrexate 20 mg weekly and adalimumab; joints are tender and swollen at the MCPs bilaterally. She also reports a 2-week history of diffuse lower abdominal and pelvic pain, crampy in nature, non-radiating. Exam: pharynx erythematous, no exudate. Abdomen soft with mild suprapubic tenderness, no rebound. Plan: supportive care for the URI, hold biologic during acute infection, continue methotrexate, urinalysis and pelvic ultrasound scheduled to evaluate pelvic pain, follow-up in 2 weeks.

Telehealth visit: 82-year-old male with recurrent unilateral throbbing headaches with photophobia and nausea, consistent with migraine, occurring about twice monthly. Also reports loud snoring, witnessed apneas, and daytime sleepiness; Epworth score 15; prior sleep study consistent with obstructive sleep apnea, but CPAP adherence poor. Plan: trial of sumatriptan at headache onset, sleep hygiene counseling, CPAP mask refit with desensitization program, follow-up sleep medicine in 6 weeks. No red-flag features on review.

49-year-old female admitted to the ward with sudden-onset dyspnea, pleuritic right chest pain, and tachycardia 118. CT pulmonary angiography confirms a filling defect in the right lower lobe pulmonary artery consistent with pulmonary embolism; started on heparin drip transitioning to apixaban. She carries a history of combat-related trauma with nightmares, hypervigilance, avoidance of crowds, and flashbacks consistent with post-traumatic stress disorder; symptoms recently intensified during hospitalization. Mental health consulted; continued sertraline 100 mg, prazosin at night for nightmares. Monitoring: serial troponins normal, repeat imaging not required. Plan: complete anticoagulation course, outpatient PTSD psychotherapy resumed on discharge, follow-up hematology and psychiatry.

Urgent care visit. 48-year-old male presents with 6 days of facial pressure over the maxillary area, purulent nasal discharge, and low-grade fever. Symptoms began after an upper respiratory infection. Denies vision changes or severe headache. Exam: temperature 100.4 F, tenderness to palpation over both maxillary sinuses, turbinate edema with yellow-green drainage, postnasal drip noted on oropharyngeal exam. Clinical picture consistent with acute bacterial sinusitis. Started amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 mg twice daily x 10 days, fluticasone nasal spray, saline rinses, and ibuprofen PRN. Return if symptoms worsen or fail to improve within 72 hours.

Telehealth follow-up. 32-year-old female presents for review of abnormal lipid panel. Total cholesterol 268 mg/dL, LDL 182 mg/dL, triglycerides 210 mg/dL, HDL 44 mg/dL — hyperlipidemia consistent with a disorder of lipoprotein metabolism. Family history of early coronary disease in her father. No chest pain or claudication. Plan: continue lifestyle counseling regarding diet and exercise, initiate atorvastatin 20 mg nightly, repeat lipid panel and hepatic panel in three months. She will complete a baseline CK and follow up by message with results.

Outpatient behavioral health clinic: 56-year-old male veteran seen for ongoing nightmares, hypervigilance, avoidance of crowds, and flashbacks related to a motor vehicle accident two years ago; symptoms consistent with post-traumatic stress disorder, CAPS-5 elevated. He additionally reports chronic inattention, forgetfulness, and restlessness dating back to childhood, and prior records support adult ADHD; he has been off stimulants for a year. Exam: alert, anxious, startle response notable, no acute distress otherwise. Plan: trauma-focused CPT sessions weekly, prazosin for nightmares, and restart low-dose extended-release stimulant with monitoring. No other medical complaints; physical exam unremarkable. Follow up in 3 weeks; crisis line reviewed.

Outpatient clinic follow-up. 23-year-old female seen after hospitalization for an ischemic stroke of the left MCA territory; MRI confirmed cerebral infarction; residual mild right-hand weakness, on aspirin and atorvastatin, physical therapy ongoing. She has a history of post-traumatic stress disorder with nightmares, hypervigilance, and avoidance; trauma-focused therapy continues, sertraline maintained. Today she also complains of sore throat and painful swallowing without cough; exam shows erythematous pharynx with exudate, rapid strep negative — acute pharyngitis, likely viral; supportive care advised. BMI 27; nutrition referral placed for overweight. Plan: continue stroke secondary prevention, PTSD care, return if symptoms worsen.

Telehealth follow-up, Internal Medicine. 71-year-old female with obesity, BMI 34.2, weight 92 kg; weight-management plan ongoing. DEXA scan last month confirmed osteoporosis (T-score -3.1 at lumbar spine) without any fracture; she is on calcium, vitamin D, and alendronate weekly. She also reports urinary frequency, weak stream, and nocturia x2; prostate exam previously showed smooth enlargement consistent with benign prostatic hyperplasia, and she has been tolerating tamsulosin 0.4 mg nightly with improvement. Note: patient is a transgender woman with prior documentation of BPH; urology follows this. Plan: continue alendronate, repeat DEXA in 2 years; continue tamsulosin; structured weight loss program with nutrition counseling and activity goals; follow up in 3 months.

Primary care clinic. 37-year-old female evaluated for fatigue, exertional dyspnea, and pica (ice craving) for several months. Heavy menstrual bleeding reported. Labs: hemoglobin 9.1, MCV 68, ferritin 4, iron saturation low — consistent with iron deficiency anemia. Exam: pallor of conjunctivae, tachycardia 102, no other findings. Plan: oral iron replacement twice daily, vitamin C to aid absorption, dietary counseling; gynecology referral for evaluation of menorrhagia; repeat CBC and ferritin in 8 weeks; colon evaluation deferred given age and clear risk factors.

Ward note, 78-year-old female admitted from home with worsening confusion. Family reports several years of progressive memory decline, disorientation, and difficulty with daily tasks; now frequently agitated in the evenings. Exam: disoriented to time and place, MMSE 14/30, no focal neurologic deficits. Neuroimaging shows diffuse cortical atrophy with hippocampal sparing pattern consistent with Alzheimer disease. She has also been clutching her lower abdomen; exam shows diffuse lower abdominal and pelvic tenderness without rebound; urinalysis and plain films unremarkable, CT abdomen pending to evaluate the abdominal and pelvic pain. Currently on donepezil 10 mg daily. Plan: continue donepezil, scheduled acetaminophen for comfort, complete abdominal workup, fall precautions, and family education.

Clinic visit, 25-year-old woman with several months of fatigue, exertional dyspnea, and heavy menstrual bleeding. Reports chronic abdominal pain relieved by defecation, alternating constipation and diarrhea consistent with irritable bowel syndrome; no alarm features. Also three days of urinary frequency, dysuria, and suprapubic burning. Exam: pallor of conjunctivae, soft abdomen with mild LLQ tenderness, no rebound. Labs: hemoglobin 9.2 g/dL, ferritin 4 ng/mL, MCV 72. UA shows pyuria and positive nitrites. Plan: start ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily, continue low-FODMAP dietary counseling and hyoscyamine PRN for IBS, and begin nitrofurantoin for the urinary tract infection. Repeat CBC in six weeks.

82M seen in primary care clinic for follow-up of multiple issues. Has history of hypothyroidism after prior thyroid radioablation years ago; on levothyroxine 75 mcg daily, TSH today mildly elevated at 8.2, dose increased to 88 mcg. Reports fatigue and cold intolerance. Longstanding alcohol dependence — drinks a pint of spirits daily, prior withdrawal seizure; continues weekly counseling, referred again for AUD program, discussed naltrexone. Also chronic plaque psoriasis with scaly erythematous plaques over extensor elbows and knees; continuing clobetasol ointment BID and reviewing phototherapy options. Plan: repeat TSH in 8 weeks, liver panel, abstinence counseling, dermatology referral.

Neurology clinic, 36-year-old male with 2-year history of resting tremor, bradykinesia, and cogwheel rigidity; diagnosed Parkinson disease, on carbidopa-levodopa with symptomatic improvement. Also reports bilateral calf pain when walking, absent pedal pulses, ABI 0.68, consistent with peripheral vascular disease; started on aspirin and statin, walking program advised. Liver ultrasound performed for mild transaminase elevation showed steatosis; workup negative for viral or alcoholic etiology, consistent with fatty liver. Weight and dietary counseling given. Levodopa schedule adjusted to three times daily. Follow-up in 4 weeks; vascular lab and repeat LFTs scheduled.

49-year-old woman seen on the hospital ward for follow-up. She was admitted three days ago with acute dyspnea and pleuritic chest pain; CT pulmonary angiogram confirmed a clot in the right lower lobe pulmonary artery, and she was started on apixaban. She has longstanding type 1 diabetes mellitus managed with an insulin pump; glucose logs reviewed and basal rates adjusted. She also reports chronic mid-back dorsalgia, worse with prolonged standing, attributed to muscular strain; physical exam shows paravertebral tenderness without neurologic deficits. Plan: continue anticoagulation, endocrinology to follow insulin dosing, NSAIDs as needed for back pain, repeat chest imaging prior to discharge.

ED note, 53-year-old male with 1 hour of crushing substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm, diaphoresis, and nausea. EMS ECG shows ST elevations in leads II, III, and aVF. Troponin I markedly elevated at 8.2 ng/mL, consistent with an acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction of the inferior wall. Immediate activation of the cath lab; aspirin 325 mg, ticagrelor 180 mg, and heparin bolus given. Emergent coronary angiography shows 100% occlusion of the right coronary artery, treated with drug-eluting stent and thrombus aspiration; flow restored. Post-PCI ECG shows resolving ST segments. Admitted to CCU. Plan: dual antiplatelet therapy, high-intensity statin, beta-blocker and ACE inhibitor as tolerated, echocardiogram, and cardiac rehabilitation referral.

Urgent care visit: 30-year-old male with four days of productive cough with clear sputum, low-grade malaise, and chest tightness. No fever, no dyspnea at rest. Exam: lungs with scattered bilateral wheezes, no crackles, no consolidation signs, oxygen saturation 98%, afebrile. Chest x-ray not indicated; clinical picture consistent with acute bronchitis. Plan: supportive care with fluids, rest, honey and dextromethorphan for cough, albuterol inhaler PRN for wheeze, return precautions for fever, worsening dyspnea, or symptoms beyond three weeks. No antibiotics indicated.

Internal medicine clinic. 70-year-old male with 5 days of diffuse myalgias, subjective chills, low-grade temperature of 100.2 F, and fatigue; rapid flu and COVID tests negative, exam without focal findings, treated as a viral infection of unspecified site with supportive care only. He also has hyperlipidemia — LDL 155 mg/dL on today's panel — for which atorvastatin 20 mg is continued. He reports occasional left lower quadrant discomfort and a prior colonoscopy with CT showing diverticulosis; diverticular disease of the intestine without acute complications, advised high-fiber diet and adequate hydration. Plan: rest, fluids, acetaminophen as needed, repeat lipid panel in 3 months, return sooner if fever worsens or abdominal pain localizes.

Internal medicine clinic. 73-year-old female presents with fatigue, decreased energy over several months, and feeling low. She reports persistent depressed mood, anhedonia, poor sleep, and weight loss — consistent with a major depressive episode, single episode; PHQ-9 score 16. Labs show hemoglobin 9.8 with low MCV-normal indices and low serum iron studies not diagnostic of a specific anemia type; being evaluated further by hematology, currently labeled unspecified anemia. Also reports recurrent left lower quadrant discomfort; CT from last month demonstrated multiple sigmoid diverticula without acute inflammation, consistent with diverticular disease. Plan: start sertraline 25 mg daily with titration, iron supplementation, high-fiber diet, repeat CBC in four weeks, hematology referral, psychiatry follow-up, return sooner if abdominal pain worsens or fever develops.

Hospital admission note. 74-year-old male presents with 24 hours of right lower quadrant pain, anorexia, nausea; exam shows localized RLQ tenderness with rebound; CT abdomen confirms acute appendicitis, scheduled for laparoscopic appendectomy. PMH significant for coronary artery disease on aspirin and atorvastatin with prior stenting and stable chronic angina pattern, obesity with BMI 32.4, and chronic migraines treated with propranolol prophylaxis. Cardiology consulted preoperatively; ECG unchanged from baseline. Plan: appendectomy tonight, continue cardiac medications, monitor migraine triggers postop, nutrition consult for weight management prior to discharge.

Clinic visit, Neurology. 57-year-old woman with recurrent unilateral throbbing headaches with photophobia, nausea, and visual aura, occurring 3-4 times monthly, consistent with migraine; sumatriptan aborts most attacks. She also reports chronic bilateral knee pain with crepitus and stiffness worsened by stairs; prior radiographs showed joint space narrowing. Takes naproxen as needed. Additionally noted is long-standing leg discomfort and heaviness with exercise due to impaired lower extremity circulation; venous duplex previously abnormal. Exam: tenderness over medial knee compartments, mild ankle edema, diminished but present pulses. Plan: continue triptan, add daily prophylaxis with topiramate; knee OA managed with NSAIDs, PT referral; compression stockings and follow-up vascular studies for peripheral vascular disease.

Clinic note, 24-year-old female with 3 months of palpitations, heat intolerance, tremor, and 8-lb weight loss. Exam: HR 104, fine tremor, mild proptosis, smooth diffuse goiter; TSH <0.01 with elevated free T4, consistent with thyrotoxicosis, Graves pattern. Also evaluated for recurrent left lower quadrant discomfort; CT colonography shows sigmoid diverticula without evidence of inflammation or perforation, consistent with diverticulosis of the colon. Additionally has well-demarcated erythematous scaly plaques with silvery scale on elbows and scalp, consistent with plaque psoriasis. Plan: start methimazole and propranolol; high-fiber diet and stool softener for diverticular disease; continue topical clobetasol for psoriasis flares; repeat thyroid function tests in 6 weeks; dermatology referral if psoriasis refractory.

Telehealth visit, general internal medicine. 67-year-old woman here for review of chronic problems. Unspecified anemia followed for years, hemoglobin 10.4 g/dL with low-normal indices; continues oral iron intermittently. Peripheral vascular disease with claudication in both calves after one block, diminished dorsalis pedis pulses, ABI 0.7; on aspirin and supervised walking program. Diverticular disease of the colon documented on prior colonoscopy, with intermittent left lower quadrant discomfort but no fever or bleeding. Benign prostatic hyperplasia with nocturia twice nightly and weak stream; on tamsulosin 0.4 mg nightly with improvement. Exam (limited, video): no distress. Plan: repeat CBC in 6 weeks, continue antiplatelet therapy, high-fiber diet for diverticulosis, continue alpha-blocker, uroflowmetry if symptoms progress.

85M presents to geriatric clinic. Longstanding attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, previously untreated, with persistent distractibility, impulsivity, and difficulty completing tasks per family report; started on low-dose methylphenidate with modest benefit. Also complains of retrosternal burning after meals and sour taste at night, consistent with gastro-esophageal reflux disease; improves with pantoprazole. Exam: unremarkable abdomen, no alarm features. Plan: continue PPI, counsel on upright positioning after meals and smaller dinners, titrate stimulant cautiously given age, follow up in 6 weeks, consider neuropsychological testing to confirm ADHD severity.

73-year-old male seen in endocrinology clinic. Evaluated for unintentional 12-pound weight loss, palpitations, heat intolerance, and tremor over three months. Exam: mild diffuse thyromegaly without nodularity, fine tremor of outstretched hands, resting HR 104 and regular, no exophthalmos. Labs: TSH <0.01, free T4 2.9, consistent with thyrotoxicosis; started on methimazole 10 mg daily with beta-blockade for symptoms, repeat labs in six weeks. He also reports epigastric burning after meals; recent EGD showed mild antral gastrism and duodenitis without ulcer; on pantoprazole 40 mg daily with improvement. Additionally complains of diffuse myalgia and aching in both thighs and calves, attributed to soft tissue/muscle pain, likely thyroid-related; NSAIDs as needed, monitor. Avoid excess iodine. Follow-up with labs and symptom review in six weeks.

Telehealth visit. 26-year-old female with hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 100 mcg daily (TSH 6.8 at last check, dose adjustment pending) presents for follow-up of diffuse myalgias and bilateral limb pain, worse in forearms and thighs, without weakness or joint swelling. Also reports recurrent upper abdominal burning managed previously with famotidine, and cognitive concerns; she is a young-onset Alzheimer disease patient under neurology care on donepezil, with progressive memory decline noted by her caregiver. Exam limited by video; no focal findings reported; intact extremities by history. Plan: increase levothyroxine to 112 mcg daily, repeat TSH in 6 weeks; restart PPI for gastritis/duodenitis symptoms; NSAID avoidance, physical therapy referral for soft tissue myalgia; neurology follow-up for cognitive decline.

Endocrinology clinic. 60-year-old male with thyrotoxicosis confirmed by suppressed TSH <0.01, elevated free T4, and diffuse uptake on thyroid scan consistent with Graves disease. Reports palpitations, weight loss, heat intolerance, and tremor. Started on methimazole 10 mg daily with beta blockade as needed. Lipid panel notable for elevated LDL 165 mg/dL and triglycerides 210 mg/dL; hyperlipidemia to be addressed after thyroid normalization since thyrotoxicosis affects lipid metabolism, but statin therapy initiated given risk profile. Creatinine 1.8 with eGFR 38, stable over 6 months, consistent with stage 3b chronic kidney disease; nephrology co-management, dose-adjusted medications, avoidance of NSAIDs. Repeat thyroid function and renal panel in 6 weeks.

82M seen in cardiology clinic for follow-up of his rate-controlled atrial fibrillation with episodes of flutter documented on prior telemetry. Reports occasional palpitations and exertional dyspnea. On apixaban and metoprolol. Exam: irregularly irregular pulse, 78 bpm; mild ankle edema. Labs this visit: creatinine 2.1 mg/dL, eGFR 32 mL/min, consistent with his known stage 4 chronic kidney disease; potassium 4.8. ECG shows atrial fibrillation without acute ischemic changes. Plan: continue anticoagulation with renal-appropriate apixaban dosing, maintain beta blocker, repeat renal panel in 2 weeks, nephrology co-management, TTE if symptoms progress.

Telehealth visit: 66-year-old female for follow-up of attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder diagnosed last year after lifelong inattention, disorganization, and restlessness. On lisdexamfetamine 30 mg each morning with good response; she reports improved task completion but some afternoon rebound distractibility. No chest pain, insomnia, or appetite loss. She has established care with a therapist for executive-function coaching. Plan: increase lisdexamfetamine to 40 mg daily, monitor blood pressure and sleep, refill prescription, and follow up by telehealth in eight weeks; continue behavioral strategies.

Hospital ward note. 86-year-old female admitted with fever, rigors, hypotension, and confusion; lactate 3.8, WBC 16,500, cultures drawn from indwelling catheter; treated as sepsis of urinary origin with IV antibiotics and fluids. She has known thyrotoxicosis with suppressed TSH and elevated free T4, maintained on methimazole, currently tremulous with HR 104; endocrinology consulted. Vitamin D 25-OH level 12 ng/mL; started cholecalciferol. Also noted coldness of the feet with absent pedal pulses and an ankle-brachial index of 0.6, consistent with peripheral arterial disease of the lower extremities; vascular service consulted, aspirin continued. Plan: monitor hemodynamics, repeat lactate, de-escalate antibiotics with culture results.

ED to inpatient admission. 38-year-old male brought in with fever, chills, productive cough with rust-colored sputum, and pleuritic right-sided chest pain for three days. History notable for heavy daily alcohol use, roughly a pint of liquor daily for ten years, with prior withdrawal seizures; he reports morning shakes and drinking to prevent tremor. Exam: temperature 101.8F, tachycardic, decreased breath sounds with crackles at right lower lobe. Chest x-ray: dense right lower lobe infiltrate. Blood cultures, sputum Gram stain sent; empiric ceftriaxone and azithromycin started for community-acquired pneumonia. Thiamine, folate, and multivitamin given; CIWA protocol initiated for alcohol withdrawal with lorazepam as needed. Incentive spirometry, daily CIWA monitoring, and addiction medicine consult for alcohol use disorder arranged.

32-year-old male at walk-in clinic. Five days of thick green nasal discharge, frontal and maxillary pressure, fever to 100.9 and reduced smell, consistent with acute sinusitis. He also reports a known history of colonic diverticulosis found on prior colonoscopy, with occasional bloating and left lower quadrant cramping; today his abdomen is soft with mild LLQ tenderness, no fever pattern to suggest diverticulitis. Plan: amoxicillin-clavulanate 875/125 BID x 10 days, decongestants, nasal saline; for the diverticular disease, continue high-fiber diet and hydration; return for worsening abdominal pain or peritoneal signs.

Stroke unit admission. 68-year-old male with sudden onset of left-sided weakness and slurred speech approximately 90 minutes prior to arrival; last known well documented. CT head showed no hemorrhage, CT angiogram revealed right middle cerebral artery occlusion consistent with acute ischemic cerebral infarction. Thrombolytics administered and thrombectomy performed with partial recanalization. NIHSS improved from 14 to 8. Admitted to neurocritical care, blood pressure permissive targets, started on aspirin and high-intensity statin. Physical, occupational, and speech therapy consulted. Swallow evaluation pending before oral intake. Monitor for hemorrhagic conversion with repeat imaging at 24 hours.

18-year-old female seen in clinic after ED visit for left calf DVT confirmed on doppler ultrasound; started on apixaban. She reports excessive daytime sleepiness, loud snoring, and witnessed pauses in breathing at night; Epworth score elevated and she is referred for polysomnography for suspected obstructive sleep apnea. She also describes diffuse myalgia and bilateral leg pain, worse after activity, without joint swelling or weakness; exam shows tender muscles without erythema or focal findings, attributed to soft tissue strain. Plan: continue anticoagulation, sleep study scheduled, gentle stretching and warm compresses for the limb pain, avoid estrogen-containing contraceptives, and follow up in four weeks.

Rheumatology clinic. 27-year-old male referred for six months of symmetrical morning stiffness lasting over an hour in the metacarpophalangeal joints, wrists, and knees, with soft tissue swelling. RF positive at 68, anti-CCP positive, elevated CRP — seropositive rheumatoid arthritis, other than classic adult type given atypical early presentation with overlapping features; methotrexate 15 mg weekly with folic acid initiated, hydroxychloroquine added. Incidental finding on labs: total cholesterol 232, LDL 154, triglycerides 210 — hyperlipidemia, likely disease and steroid-sparing treatment related; dietary counseling given, statin therapy deferred pending repeat panel in three months. Hand X-rays show soft tissue swelling without erosions. Ophthalmology baseline exam arranged for hydroxychloroquine. Follow-up in six weeks with repeat inflammatory markers.

72M admitted to hospital ward via ED with acute kidney failure. Creatinine 3.6 mg/dL (baseline 1.1), BUN 48, oliguria 400 mL/24h. Urinalysis bland, renal ultrasound without obstruction; diagnosed acute kidney injury presumed prerenal/volume-related, treated with IV fluids, holding nephrotoxic agents, daily creatinine trending down. Pulmonary issues: chronic asthma with intermittent wheeze, using albuterol inhaler frequently; heard expiratory wheezing on exam. Restarted inhaled budesonide-formoterol, prednisone burst for asthma exacerbation avoided high dose given renal status. No pneumothorax on chest x-ray. Nephrology consulted for AKI management. Discharge planned when creatinine below 2.0 and urine output adequate; follow-up with PCP and repeat BMP in 1 week.

Pulmonary clinic. 65-year-old male with asthma since childhood, currently using an albuterol inhaler two to three times weekly and nighttime awakenings twice monthly; started on a low-dose inhaled corticosteroid with spacer, and peak expiratory flow monitoring reviewed. He also reports cramping pain in both calves after walking one block, relieved by rest, over the past year. Exam: diminished posterior tibial and dorsalis pedis pulses, loss of lower leg hair, cool feet; ankle-brachial indices 0.7 bilaterally consistent with peripheral vascular disease. Already on a statin; added aspirin, counseled on foot care and a supervised walking regimen. Plan: asthma follow-up in 6 weeks with spirometry, vascular lab surveillance, and return sooner for rest pain or non-healing wounds.

ED note. 45-year-old male with BMI 33 presenting with acute onset right-sided pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea. History of obstructive sleep apnea on CPAP, noncompliant lately. CT pulmonary angiogram: acute subsegmental pulmonary embolism right lower lobe. Hemodynamically stable, troponin negative. Started on rivaroxaban 15 mg twice daily. Obesity noted as contributing risk factor; encouraged weight reduction and CPAP adherence. Plan: discharge on anticoagulation with hematology follow-up, repeat d-dimer in 3 months, return precautions for worsening dyspnea, hemoptysis, or syncope. Sleep medicine contacted to reinforce CPAP refit.

Urgent care. 26-year-old male with type 1 diabetes presents with 3 days of sore throat, painful swallowing, and fever to 101.2 F. No cough. Uses insulin glargine and lispro via pump; last A1c 7.1%. Checks glucose frequently; no vomiting, tolerating fluids. Exam: T 100.8 F, pharynx erythematous with tonsillar exudates, tender anterior cervical adenopathy, rapid strep positive. Impression: acute streptococcal pharyngitis in a T1DM patient. Plan: penicillin VK 500 mg BID x 10 days, antipyretics, continue basal-bolus insulin with sick-day rules and ketone checks, follow up if unable to keep fluids down.

ED note: 85-year-old male brought in by ambulance with 24 hours of anorexia, nausea, and right lower quadrant pain, first noticed after a fall that also triggered a flare of his long-standing combat-related PTSD with nightmares, hypervigilance, and flashbacks requiring staff to approach slowly. Exam: RLQ tenderness with guarding, positive Rovsing sign, WBC 15.8, CT abdomen showing a dilated appendix with periappendiceal fat stranding — acute appendicitis. Surgery consulted; given his age, planned laparoscopic appendectomy tonight. Behavioral health consulted to continue his sertraline and provide support during hospitalization. Plan: NPO, IV antibiotics, OR, PTSD symptom monitoring on the ward.

Inpatient ward note. 79-year-old male admitted with three days of fevers, malaise, and diffuse myalgias; rapid influenza and COVID testing negative, workup unrevealing, clinically felt to be a viral infection of unspecified site; supportive care with fluids and antipyretics. On hospital day two he developed left calf swelling and tenderness; duplex ultrasound showed an acute left lower extremity deep venous thrombosis. Started on therapeutic enoxaparin transitioning to apixaban. He also reports generalized myalgia and bilateral limb pain attributed to soft tissue strain, managed with acetaminophen and gentle mobility. Hematology consulted. Monitor for pulmonary embolism symptoms, repeat CBC and renal function.

ICU admission note. 70-year-old man transferred from outside hospital with altered mental status and fever. Found hypotensive, tachycardic, temp 38.9, lactate 4.2, WBC 18,000; blood cultures grew Gram-negative rods — sepsis with acute organ dysfunction, source suspected urinary. He was also found to have acute left-sided weakness; MRI confirms an acute right MCA territory ischemic infarction, likely embolic. Exam: lethargic but arousable, left hemiparesis 2/5, left facial droop, left neglect. Plan: sepsis bundle — broad-spectrum antibiotics, fluid resuscitation, vasopressors as needed; aspirin deferred until acute issues clarify per neurology; stroke protocol with head-of-bed positioning, swallow evaluation, physical and occupational therapy; repeat cultures, daily neuro checks, DVT prophylaxis, family meeting scheduled.

82-year-old woman admitted to the medical ward. She presents with palpitations, tremor, heat intolerance, 8-lb weight loss, and TSH suppressed at 0.02 with elevated free T4, consistent with thyrotoxicosis; thyroid uptake suggests toxic nodular goiter. She describes chronic excessive worry, restlessness, poor sleep, and recurrent panic attacks with chest tightness, consistent with generalized anxiety disorder with panic attacks. She also reports two days of sore throat without exudate, consistent with acute pharyngitis, and has a history of asthma with intermittent wheeze; she uses albuterol as needed. Plan: methimazole, propranolol for rate and anxiety symptoms, sertraline continuation, saltwater gargles, albuterol, endocrinology follow-up.

Clinic SOAP: 49-year-old female with 4 days of sore throat, nasal congestion, dry cough, and low-grade fever to 100.4. No chest pain or dyspnea. Exam: T 100.2, pharynx mildly erythematous without exudate, tender anterior cervical lymphadenopathy, lungs clear, no focal consolidation. Rapid strep negative, flu negative. Impression: acute viral upper respiratory infection. Plan: supportive care with fluids, rest, acetaminophen, saline nasal rinses; return if symptoms worsen, fever persists beyond 5 days, or shortness of breath develops. Work note provided for 2 days.

Endocrinology clinic visit. 79-year-old man with longstanding type 1 diabetes since age 30, on basal-bolus insulin (glargine at night, lispro with meals). Reports occasional morning hypoglycemia; glucose log shows fasting values 90-140. A1c today 7.4%. Also here for lipid management — history of mixed hyperlipidemia with elevated LDL and triglycerides; on atorvastatin 40 mg daily, lipid panel today shows LDL 92, triglycerides 210, HDL 38. Exam: no foot ulcers, monofilament sensation intact, mild retinopathy on fundoscopic exam. Plan: reduce glargine by 2 units, continue carbohydrate counting education, add omega-3 supplementation, intensify statin therapy, repeat lipid panel in three months, annual retinal screening, nutritionist referral for both glycemic and lipid control.

56-year-old female seen in family medicine clinic for review of bone density results. Postmenopausal for four years; DEXa scan shows T-score -2.7 at the total hip and -2.9 at the lumbar spine, confirming osteoporosis. No fractures, no height loss, no kyphosis; vertebral fracture assessment negative. Exam: normal gait, no spinal tenderness. Calcium and vitamin D levels adequate. Initiated alendronate 70 mg weekly with instructions to take upright with a full glass of water and remain upright 30 minutes; continue calcium 1000 mg and vitamin D 1000 IU daily. Counseling on fall prevention, weight-bearing and resistance exercise, limiting alcohol. Repeat DEXA in two years. Return sooner for any new back pain or suspected fracture.

Urgent care note. 49-year-old woman presents with 5 days of productive cough and low-grade fever; lungs clear to auscultation with scattered rhonchi, no consolidation — clinical picture of acute bronchitis. Supportive care advised, guaifenesin, no antibiotics indicated. She also reports epigastric burning and nausea for the past week; history of gastritis and duodenitis on prior endoscopy, currently flaring; omeprazole 20 mg daily restarted, avoid NSAIDs. Additionally, longstanding excessive daytime sleepiness, loud snoring with witnessed pauses; home sleep study consistent with obstructive sleep apnea, using CPAP with variable adherence. Plan: rest, fluids, return if fever persists; continue PPI for 8 weeks; CPAP compliance review and sleep clinic follow-up; return in 2 weeks.

Clinic SOAP: 33-year-old female with epilepsy since adolescence, well controlled on lamotrigine 200 mg BID, no seizures in 14 months; levels therapeutic. Presents today with two weeks of gnawing epigastric pain, worse with meals, mild nausea, no melena or hematemesis; H. pylori stool antigen positive. Impression: recurrent seizures (stable) and H. pylori-associated gastritis with duodenitis. Plan: continue lamotrigine, begin triple therapy with amoxicillin, clarithromycin, and omeprazole for 14 days, avoid NSAIDs, repeat stool antigen after 6 weeks, seizure diary, annual lamotrigine level, follow-up in 4 weeks.

Urgent care note. 34-year-old man presents with three days of productive cough, fever to 101.5, pleuritic right-sided chest pain. Chest X-ray shows a right lower lobe infiltrate; no organism identified on culture yet — treating as community-acquired pneumonia with amoxicillin-clavulanate. He reports easy fatigue and dyspnea on minimal exertion out of proportion to illness; CBC shows hemoglobin 9.8 with low MCHC, consistent with anemia, type to be determined with iron studies and hemoglobin electrophoresis pending. BMI today 31.4, in the obese range; we discussed diet and gradual exercise plan. He also describes months of excessive worry, muscle tension, and two recent episodes of sudden pounding heartbeat and fear of dying in public settings, consistent with generalized anxiety with panic attacks. Plan: antibiotics, anemia workup, weight management counseling, escitalopram start, psychology referral for CBT.

Endocrinology clinic. 22-year-old man referred for 3 months of palpitations, heat intolerance, weight loss of 12 pounds, tremor, and difficulty sleeping. Exam: pulse 112 regular, mild proptosis, warm moist skin, fine hand tremor, thyroid diffusely enlarged and smooth without nodularity, no bruit. Labs: suppressed TSH <0.01, free T4 elevated at 3.4, consistent with thyrotoxicosis; TSI antibodies pending to characterize the etiology. ECG shows sinus tachycardia only. Assessment: hyperthyroidism, thyrotoxic state. Plan: start methimazole 10 mg daily and propranolol 20 mg TID for symptom control, endocrine ultrasound, repeat thyroid function tests in 4 weeks, counsel on smoking-free status and symptom red flags.

Skilled nursing facility telehealth visit. 86-year-old female with multiple comorbidities. Recent MRI confirms chronic changes of an old cerebral infarction involving the left middle cerebral artery territory; residual right-sided weakness and aphasia, continuing physical, occupational, and speech therapy. TSH elevated at 12.4 on recent labs; other hypothyroidism being managed with levothyroxine 50 mcg daily, dose increased with repeat levels in 6 weeks. Liver ultrasound shows hepatic steatosis; LFTs mildly elevated, consistent with fatty liver disease, weight management and alcohol avoidance discussed. She also carries a PTSD diagnosis related to earlier life trauma, with anxiety and sleep disturbance; psychological services continuing and prazosin at bedtime. Family updated on overall plan.

37M seen in neurology clinic with 2-year decline in short-term memory — repeats questions, misplaced wallet multiple times, got lost driving familiar route; wife notes personality change and word-finding difficulty. MoCA 18/30. MRI shows early hippocampal atrophy; extensive workup negative for reversible causes. Diagnosis: early-onset Alzheimer disease, likely familial given father affected at 45. Started donepezil 5 mg daily titrating to 10 mg; discussion of memantine later; genetic counseling referral for family. Also has chronic plaque psoriasis with well-demarcated scaly plaques on scalp, elbows, and lower back, intermittently treated; topical clobetasol and calcipotriene prescribed, dermatology follow-up for phototherapy if refractory. Caregiver support resources provided, driving safety counseling, return in 3 months with repeat cognitive testing.

Urgent care visit. 48-year-old male with 2 days of sore throat, painful swallowing, and low-grade fever. No cough. Exam: pharynx erythematous with tonsillar exudates, tender anterior cervical nodes, temperature 37.9 C. Rapid strep negative; clinical picture consistent with acute pharyngitis, treated symptomatically with salt-water gargles and analgesics. Patient acknowledges ongoing heavy daily alcohol use with prior withdrawal symptoms; meets criteria for alcohol use disorder. Brief intervention performed, referral to addiction medicine and support group given, lab monitoring advised. Return if symptoms worsen or no improvement in one week.

Vascular clinic. 31-year-old male referred for bilateral leg discomfort. Reports aching and heaviness in both lower extremities, worse with standing, improved with elevation. Exam reveals dilated, tortuous superficial veins with reticular changes over both calves, mild ankle edema, intact pulses, no ulceration. Venous duplex shows chronic superficial venous insufficiency with reflux; findings consistent with chronic venous disorder of the lower extremities. No arterial disease. Plan: graduated compression stockings 30-40 mmHg, lifestyle counseling on leg elevation, consideration of ultrasound-guided sclerotherapy in three months if symptoms persist. Follow-up vascular visit in 12 weeks.

Internal medicine clinic. 47-year-old female with hyperlipidemia — LDL 168, total cholesterol 240 — started on atorvastatin 20 mg; repeat lipid panel in 3 months. Presents today with a painful, spreading erythematous, warm plaque on the left calf with streaking toward the knee, consistent with cellulitis with acute lymphangitis; afebrile, no abscess on ultrasound; started on cephalexin 500 mg four times daily for 7 days with elevation and marking of margins. Also known osteoporosis without current pathological fracture — DEXA T-score -2.8 at the femoral neck — continuing calcium, vitamin D, and alendronate weekly. Plan: recheck cellulitis in 48 hours, repeat DEXA in two years, fall prevention counseling.

ED note: 46-year-old male brought in by ambulance after a generalized tonic-clonic seizure; he has known epilepsy on levetiracetam but ran out of his medication last week. While in the department he developed right lower quadrant abdominal pain with anorexia and rebound tenderness; CT abdomen revealed acute appendicitis. Labs also show creatinine 2.1 mg/dL, consistent with his known chronic kidney disease, stage 3b. Plan: neurology consultation, resume antiepileptic with loading dose, general surgery consulted for appendectomy, nephrology aware given CKD for perioperative dosing and contrast avoidance, admit to surgical ward.

Urology clinic. 37-year-old male with young-onset Parkinson disease, stable on carbidopa/levodopa and pramipexole, presents with a painful, red, swollen area on his left shin of two days, now with a spreading streak of redness up toward the knee. Exam: temperature 100.8, left lower leg with a warm, erythematous, indurated plaque and linear lymphangitic streaking, tender inguinal nodes; consistent with cellulitis with acute lymphangitis. Incited by a small abrasion. Started on cephalexin 500 mg four times daily for 10 days, elevation, and marking the border; return in 48 hours or to ED for spreading, fever, or systemic symptoms. Also reports progressive urinary hesitancy, weak stream, nocturia twice nightly over the past year; exam and post-void residual consistent with benign prostatic hyperplasia; started on tamsulosin 0.4 mg nightly with uroflowmetry in six weeks. Parkinson regimen unchanged.

57-year-old male presents to ED with sudden-onset right-sided pleuritic chest pain and shortness of breath. History of urinary hesitancy and weak stream from enlarged prostate, on tamsulosin. CT pulmonary angiogram demonstrates a filling defect in the right lower lobe pulmonary artery consistent with pulmonary embolism. Started on heparin drip, transitioned to apixaban. BPH symptoms stable, continue tamsulosin; monitor for urinary retention on anticoagulation. Admitted to telemetry for anticoagulation and observation. D-dimer elevated. Plan: complete 3-6 months anticoagulation, follow-up with urology for BPH management.

ED note. 31-year-old man presents with 2 days of watery diarrhea, cramping, and low-grade fever after a questionable meal; stool studies sent, clinically infectious gastroenteritis/colitis, managed with oral rehydration and antiemetics. Past medical history notable for type 2 diabetes mellitus, on metformin 1000 mg BID, A1c 7.8% — metformin held during acute illness with instructions on sick-day rules. He also has chronic right knee pain from osteoarthritis, diagnosed radiographically last year, managed with scheduled acetaminophen and quadriceps strengthening exercises. Exam: mild diffuse abdominal tenderness without peritoneal signs; right knee with crepitus and mild effusion. Plan: discharge with oral rehydration, bland diet; resume metformin when tolerating diet; orthopedics follow-up for knee; return for dehydration or worsening symptoms.

ICU admission. 82-year-old male brought in with fever, rigors, hypotension 82/48, tachycardia 118, and confusion. Lactate 4.6, WBC 19,400; blood cultures drawn and broad-spectrum antibiotics started for sepsis of unclear source. On review he reported facial pain and purulent drainage for one week prior, consistent with acute sinusitis. Abdominal ultrasound obtained for right upper quadrant tenderness revealed multiple gallstones without cholecystitis (cholelithiasis). Aggressive fluid resuscitation given, vasopressors briefly required. ENT and general surgery consulted. Continued monitoring of mental status, urine output, and repeat lactate.

34-year-old male, weight management clinic. BMI 32 with central adiposity; exam notable for acanthosis of the neck. Liver ultrasound shows increased hepatic echogenicity consistent with hepatic steatosis; ALT mildly elevated at 68; diagnosed with nonalcoholic fatty liver disease. He also reports persistent diffuse muscle aches and bilateral thigh and forearm pain for several weeks, worse after activity, without weakness, fever, or trauma — consistent with myalgia and limb pain; CK, TSH, and inflammatory markers normal. No alcohol use. Plan: structured weight-loss program with dietitian, target 7% weight reduction, aerobic exercise 150 min/weekly, repeat liver enzymes in three months, physiotherapy referral for soft tissue pain, avoid NSAIDs given liver findings, follow-up in six weeks.

ED visit. 89-year-old male with longstanding seropositive rheumatoid arthritis on methotrexate presents with 3 days of nasal congestion, facial pressure over the maxillary sinuses, purulent rhinorrhea, sore throat, and low-grade fever — acute sinusitis superimposed on an acute upper respiratory infection; started on saline rinses and amoxicillin given duration and purulence. He also reports heavy snoring and witnessed apneas for years; prior sleep study consistent with obstructive sleep apnea, nonadherent to CPAP — re-educated and refitted mask. Rheumatoid arthritis currently stable with minimal synovitis; methotrexate continued. Discharged with ENT follow-up.

Telehealth visit, 74-year-old female presenting with months of excessive worry, difficulty concentrating, muscle tension, and poor sleep. She describes discrete episodes of palpitations, sweating, trembling, shortness of breath, and fear of dying lasting 10-20 minutes, occurring several times monthly, consistent with panic attacks. No depressive features. PHQ-9 minimal; GAD-7 score 16. No active medical illness; review of systems otherwise negative. Exam not performed (video visit); patient appears mildly restless. Plan: start sertraline 25 mg daily titrating to 50 mg, refer for CBT, relaxation techniques, sleep hygiene counseling. Follow-up telehealth in 4 weeks; return sooner if panic attacks worsen.

65-year-old woman seen in internal medicine clinic for follow-up of lifelong inattention, distractibility and impulsivity, consistent with adult ADHD; she continues lisdexamfetamine with good response. She also reports three days of left calf swelling, warmth and tenderness. Exam: left calf 3 cm larger than right, positive Homan's sign, no erythema tracking. Duplex ultrasound: acute non-occlusive thrombus in the left popliteal and tibial veins, a deep vein thrombosis. Plan: continue stimulant at current dose, start apixaban 5 mg BID, hematology referral, return precautions for dyspnea or chest pain.

Orthopedic clinic. 89-year-old female with several years of bilateral knee pain, worse with stairs and standing, morning stiffness under 30 minutes, and crepitus on exam. No swelling or warmth; varus alignment noted bilaterally. X-rays show joint space narrowing and osteophytes consistent with osteoarthritis of both knees. No history of inflammatory arthritis. Plan: continue acetaminophen, add topical diclofenac gel, quadriceps strengthening exercises with physical therapy, cane for longer walks, and weight-appropriate activity modification. Corticosteroid injection offered for the right knee if symptoms progress. Reassess in three months; discussed that knee replacement remains an option if conservative measures fail.

Telehealth visit. 58-year-old male with 4 days of myalgias, low-grade fever of 100.8 F, sore throat, headache, and nasal congestion. No focal symptoms, no chest pain, no dysuria. Exam via video: alert, no apparent distress, no rash observed. Rapid strep and COVID-19 antigen both negative; clinically felt to be a viral infection of unspecified site. Advised supportive care with fluids, rest, and acetaminophen as needed, with return precautions for worsening shortness of breath, high fever, or confusion. No antibiotics prescribed. Follow-up by phone in 3-5 days if symptoms persist.

61-year-old female admitted with 3 days of worsening dyspnea and productive cough. Known COPD on flutropium/formoterol and albuterol; exam with wheeze and prolonged expiration, treated with steroids, nebulizers, and antibiotics. She also reports chronic heartburn — longstanding reflux, on pantoprazole, continue. Admission labs notable for creatinine 2.6 from baseline 0.9 with reduced urine output — acute kidney injury from dehydration and NSAID use; held nephrotoxins, IV fluids, creatinine improving. Liver ultrasound during admission shows hepatic steatosis; LFTs mildly elevated, consistent with fatty liver disease. Abstain from alcohol, weight and diet counseling, follow-up ultrasound in 6 months. Discharged home on inhalers, PPI, and renal follow-up.

Hospital ward progress note. 77-year-old male admitted with acute ST-elevation myocardial infarction, underwent primary PCI with drug-eluting stent to the LAD; started on aspirin, ticagrelor, metoprolol, and atorvastatin. Also noted left lower leg erythema with warmth, tenderness, and a red streaking up the medial calf consistent with cellulitis with acute lymphangitis; started on IV cefazolin. History of osteoporosis on prior DXA with T-score -2.8 at the femoral neck, never fractured; continue calcium, vitamin D, and alendronate 70 mg weekly while inpatient. Cardiology and dermatology/wound checks daily. Afebrile today, leg erythema improving, troponin trending down. Plan: complete antibiotic course, cardiac rehab referral, dual antiplatelet therapy education before discharge.

Pulmonology clinic, 63-year-old male with chronic productive cough and progressive exertional dyspnea. Exam: barrel chest, diminished breath sounds, prolonged expiration. Spirometry: FEV1/FVC 0.55, minimal reversibility — consistent with his COPD; inhaler technique reviewed, continued tiotropium and albuterol, annual influenza and pneumococcal vaccination updated. Fasting lipid panel shows total cholesterol 248, LDL 168 — hyperlipidemia; started on atorvastatin 20 mg nightly with repeat panel in three months. Plan: pulmonary rehab referral, follow-up spirometry, dietary counseling.

Clinic visit, 57M here for follow-up of loud snoring, witnessed apneas, and daytime sleepiness. Overnight polysomnography showed an apnea-hypopnea index of 24 with desaturations, consistent with moderate obstructive sleep apnea. CPAP trial initiated at 8 cm H2O with good early tolerance. Also complains of recurrent itchy, scaly patches on flexor forearms and behind knees consistent with chronic eczema; exam reveals erythematous lichenified plaques. Plan: continue CPAP nightly, sleep hygiene counseling, weight-neutral advice, triamcinolone 0.1% cream BID to flares, liberal emollient use, follow-up in 6 weeks.

Hematology consult: 79-year-old female referred for fatigue and exertional dyspnea. Labs: hemoglobin 8.9 g/dL, MCV 72, ferritin 8 ng/mL, iron saturation 6% — iron deficiency anemia. Colonoscopy and upper endoscopy recently normal. Exam: pallor, brittle nails; no overt bleeding source identified. Started on oral ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily with vitamin C, iron infusion considered if intolerant. Repeat CBC and iron studies in 6 weeks. Dietary counseling regarding iron-rich foods.

Internal medicine clinic. 63-year-old female presents for follow-up of attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, diagnosed in adulthood, with persistent difficulty sustaining attention on tasks, disorganization, and impulsivity; she reports partial benefit on current methylphenidate extended-release. She also notes 3 days of progressive redness, swelling, and warmth of the left lower leg with a tender, spreading red streak up toward the inner thigh, consistent with cellulitis with acute lymphangitis; no abscess, no crepitus. She is afebrile, tender erythematous plaque over the shin with a palpable linear streak along the lymphatic channels, inguinal nodes mildly tender. Plan: increase methylphenidate dose, continue ADHD counseling; start cephalexin 500 mg four times daily for 7-10 days, elevate limb, mark erythema border, recheck in 48 hours.

75-year-old female seen at nutrition clinic for weight management. BMI 31.4, weight 172 lbs, height 66 inches. She reports gradual weight gain over the past decade since retirement, reduced activity, and frequent snacking. Exam unremarkable; waist circumference 40 inches. Vital signs normal. No other medical conditions identified; labs from last visit within normal limits. Assessment: obesity. Plan: structured Mediterranean-style diet with dietitian, target 5-10% weight loss over 6 months, walking program starting 20 minutes daily with gradual increase, behavioral counseling, follow-up in 8 weeks with weight and waist measurement.

Outpatient behavioral health clinic. 36-year-old male presents with months of persistent worry, muscle tension, restlessness, and difficulty concentrating, meeting criteria for generalized anxiety disorder. He also describes recurrent unexpected panic attacks with palpitations, sweating, trembling, and fear of dying, episodes peaking within minutes, consistent with panic disorder. No depressive symptoms, no suicidal ideation, no substance use. Started on sertraline, titrating dose, with referral for cognitive behavioral therapy. Reviewed relaxation techniques and sleep hygiene. PHQ-9 negative. Will follow up in four weeks to assess medication response and consider addition of buspirone if needed. Return sooner if panic attacks worsen or side effects develop.

Outpatient clinic. 68-year-old male with long-standing asthma presenting for follow-up. Uses albuterol rescue inhaler 2-3 times weekly, nighttime awakenings twice monthly; no oral steroid courses in past year. Exam: mild expiratory wheeze, good air movement, no accessory muscle use. Spirometry: FEV1 78% predicted with 14% bronchodilator response. Also reports recurrent abdominal pain with bloating and alternating constipation/diarrhea over 12 months, relieved by defecation, worse with stress; exam benign, no alarm features, prior labs and colonoscopy normal. Impression: asthma not optimally controlled; irritable bowel syndrome. Plan: add low-dose ICS-formoterol maintenance therapy, asthma action plan; IBS: dietary modification trial, fiber, antispasmodic PRN, reassurance; follow-up 8 weeks.

Inpatient note. 22-year-old male admitted with acute pleuritic right-sided chest pain and dyspnea. CT pulmonary angiogram shows segmental pulmonary embolism in the right lower lobe; started on apixaban. He has a history of alcohol use disorder with prior withdrawal seizure, currently enrolled in an intensive outpatient program; CIWA monitoring on admission was low-risk, continue thiamine and folate. Baseline creatinine elevated at 1.6 with eGFR 48, consistent with stage 3a chronic kidney disease; nephrology consulted, renal dosing of anticoagulation applied, hydration maintained. Plan: anticoagulation education, repeat BMP, addiction medicine follow-up, hematology to evaluate for hypercoagulable state after acute phase.

64-year-old male evaluated in vascular clinic for bilateral calf cramping with ambulation, relieved by rest, plus chronic non-healing ulcer over the left medial malleolus. Exam: diminished dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses bilaterally, trophic skin changes, dependent rubor. ABI 0.65 left, 0.72 right. Duplex shows diffuse distal arterial disease without significant stenosis of major vessels, not consistent with classic claudication from a single lesion. Assessment: peripheral vascular disease with arterial insufficiency and ischemic ulcer. Plan: wound care with compression avoidance, aspirin 81 mg daily, statin therapy, podiatry referral, smoking not an issue, aggressive wound care, repeat ABI in 3 months, discuss revascularization if ulcer fails to improve.

GI clinic. 38-year-old female with years of recurrent abdominal discomfort relieved by defecation, alternating bowel habit, and bloating — typical irritable bowel syndrome; Rome IV criteria met. She also reports postprandial right upper quadrant pain, and an ultrasound performed last week demonstrated multiple gallstones without wall thickening or ductal dilation. No fever or jaundice. Labs notable for creatinine 1.5 mg/dL, stable from prior values, eGFR 44 — consistent with stage 3a chronic kidney disease. Plan: low-FODMAP diet trial, antispasmodic PRN, discuss elective cholecystectomy given symptomatic cholelithiasis, nephrology referral for CKD management, avoid NSAIDs, repeat renal panel in 3 months.

Orthopedic clinic visit: 27-year-old female with six months of right knee pain, worse with stairs and prolonged standing, morning stiffness under 30 minutes, no preceding trauma. Exam: crepitus with flexion, mild medial joint line tenderness, stable ligaments, effusion trace. Weight-bearing radiographs show joint space narrowing and osteophytes consistent with osteoarthritis of the right knee. She also reports intermittent lower abdominal and pelvic pain over recent months, crampy in nature; abdominal exam shows mild suprapubic tenderness without rebound; pelvic pathology workup initiated with pelvic ultrasound ordered and gynecology referral. Plan: NSAIDs as needed, quadriceps strengthening and physical therapy, activity modification; follow up in 6 weeks or sooner for pelvic pain results.

ED to surgical admission. 87-year-old female with 24 hours of right lower quadrant pain, anorexia, and low-grade fever; CT abdomen shows dilated appendix with periappendiceal fat stranding and a fecalith, consistent with acute appendicitis. Exam also reveals warm erythema with spreading margins and lymphangitic streaking over the right lower leg, cellulitis with acute lymphangitis, marked for tracking. She additionally reports chronic midline dorsalgia, back pain, managed conservatively with heat and positioning; imaging unchanged from prior. Chronic kidney disease stage 3, creatinine 1.8, eGFR 40, antibiotics renally dosed. Taken for laparoscopic appendectomy; IV ceftriaxone covers both processes. Post-op plan: renal monitoring, pain control avoiding NSAIDs, ambulation, wound checks.

Hospital ward follow-up. 64-year-old woman admitted with several days of decreased urine output and rising creatinine; acute kidney injury confirmed with creatinine 3.8 mg/dL from baseline 0.9, attributed to dehydration and recent NSAID use. Home issues include chronic heartburn with retrosternal burning, worse lying flat, controlled intermittently with omeprazole; endoscopy two years ago showed erosive changes consistent with GERD. DEXA scan last year demonstrated low bone mineral density with T-score of -2.7 at the femoral neck, consistent with osteoporosis, without any fracture; she takes calcium and vitamin D supplements and was previously on alendronate. Exam: mild epigastric tenderness, no costovertebral angle tenderness. Plan: IV fluids, hold nephrotoxins, monitor renal panel; resume PPI therapy for reflux; restart bisphosphonate once renal function stabilizes; nephrology follow-up.

Pulmonology clinic. 54-year-old female with COPD on tiotropium and albuterol presents with three days of productive cough, green sputum, fever, and increased dyspnea. Exam: scattered rhonchi and crackles right lower lobe, decreased breath sounds at bases with prolonged expiration. Chest x-ray shows a right lower lobe infiltrate consistent with community-acquired pneumonia, organism not yet identified; cultures pending. Started on doxycycline and a 5-day prednisone burst, inhaler technique reviewed. She also reports bilateral knee pain with crepitus and morning stiffness; exam consistent with osteoarthritis of the knees, managed with acetaminophen and quadriceps strengthening given her lung disease. Follow-up in 1 week; return sooner if worsening hypoxia.

Dermatology clinic: 47-year-old male with recurrent itchy, scaly patches on flexor surfaces of both elbows and hands, worse in winter and with frequent hand-washing at work. Exam: erythematous, lichenified plaques with excoriations over elbows and dorsal hands; no pustules or infection. Consistent with chronic eczema; prescribed triamcinolone 0.1% ointment BID x2 weeks, liberal emollients, fragrance-free soap. He also reports diffuse shoulder and upper arm muscle soreness for several weeks after starting a manual labor job, exam shows myofascial tenderness without joint swelling — soft tissue strain; NSAIDs, stretching, and activity modification advised. Follow-up in 6 weeks or sooner if rash worsens.

Telehealth visit. 34-year-old female with two weeks of low mood, anhedonia, poor sleep, decreased appetite, and difficulty concentrating; denies suicidal ideation. PHQ-9 score 18, consistent with major depressive disorder, single episode. Started on escitalopram 10 mg daily with follow-up in four weeks. Also reports facial pressure over the maxillary region, purulent nasal discharge, and headache for five days, consistent with acute sinusitis; recommended saline irrigation, intranasal fluticasone, and supportive care. Home blood pressure logs averaging 152/94 despite lifestyle measures; essential hypertension confirmed at prior visits, amlodipine 5 mg daily started. Repeat BP check and labs in two weeks.

Pulmonology clinic. 41-year-old male with cough productive of clear sputum for the past week, chest tightness, and mild wheeze; no fever, lungs with scattered wheezing but no crackles or consolidation, felt to be acute bronchitis superimposed on his asthma. He is on albuterol HFA as needed and fluticasone-salmeterol 250/50 twice daily; peak flow today 75% of his personal best. Given the bronchitis exacerbating his asthma, prednisone 40 mg daily for 5 days was added, albuterol use increased temporarily, and he was instructed to monitor peak flows twice daily. Plan: supportive fluids and rest, return or go to ED for severe dyspnea, peak flow below 50%, or no improvement in one week; routine follow-up in 4 weeks.

56-year-old female seen in the ED with 18 hours of periumbilical pain migrating to the right lower quadrant, anorexia, fever 38.4 C, McBurney point tenderness with guarding; CT abdomen shows acute appendicitis, no perforation. Incidentally, CT demonstrates sigmoid diverticula without inflammation; she reports prior intermittent left lower quadrant discomfort consistent with diverticular disease, to be managed with fiber and follow-up. She has known COPD on tiotropium and albuterol inhalers, chronic daily sputum and exertional dyspnea; pre-op spirometry shows obstruction. Plan: laparoscopic appendectomy tonight, continue bronchodilators perioperatively, incentive spirometry, anesthesia aware of airway risk, outpatient GI counseling regarding diverticular diet after recovery.

ED presentation. 42-year-old female, known early-onset Alzheimer disease managed with donepezil, and hypothyroidism on levothyroxine 100 mcg daily (TSH checked last month, stable), brought in by husband for 14 hours of right lower quadrant pain with anorexia, nausea, and low-grade fever. Exam: RLQ tenderness with guarding, positive Rovsing sign. CT abdomen: enlarged appendix with periappendiceal fat stranding, no perforation. Labs mild leukocytosis. Diagnosis: acute appendicitis. General surgery consulted; taken for laparoscopic appendectomy. Levothyroxine continued per home regimen; donepezil held postoperatively and resumed. Husband updated on plan including her cognitive baseline for postoperative delirium monitoring.

Primary care clinic. 76-year-old female for fatigue evaluation. Labs: hemoglobin 9.8, MCV 74, ferritin 8, iron saturation 8%. Diagnosed with iron deficiency anemia; colonoscopy and EGD previously unremarkable. BMI 28.4, weight stable, counseled on diet and activity. Also has history of gout with two prior first MTP flares, uric acid 8.9, currently on allopurinol 100 mg daily. Exam: pale conjunctiva, no joint swelling today, trace ankle edema absent. Plan: ferrous sulfate 325 mg three times weekly with vitamin C, repeat CBC and ferritin in 8 weeks, continue allopurinol and titrate to uric acid goal below 6, weight management with nutrition referral, avoid iron with allopurinol dosing times.

ED note. 36-year-old male with 2 hours of crushing substernal chest pressure radiating to left arm, diaphoresis. ECG shows ST elevations in leads II, III, aVF. Troponin markedly elevated; emergent cath showed occluded right coronary artery with drug-eluting stent placed. Started on aspirin, ticagrelor, metoprolol, atorvastatin. Also noted chronic pruritic, erythematous scaly patches on flexor forearms consistent with eczema, managed with triamcinolone cream and antihistamine. Admitted to cardiology for post-MI monitoring.

Rheumatology clinic. 35-year-old female referred for low bone density after a fragility workup. DEXA scan shows lumbar spine T-score of -2.7 and hip -2.5, consistent with osteoporosis; no current or prior fracture, imaging confirms no compression deformity. Likely related to long-standing glucocorticoid exposure for autoimmune disease and hypoestrogenism. Started on alendronate 70 mg weekly with calcium and vitamin D supplementation; steroid taper being coordinated with rheumatology. Weight-bearing exercise and fall prevention counseling provided. Repeat DEXA in two years or sooner. Fracture precautions and red-flag symptoms reviewed.

Hospital ward, infectious disease consult. 86-year-old male admitted from a nursing home with fever, hypotension, tachycardia, and confusion; blood cultures grew Escherichia coli, and lactate was 4.1 — clinical picture of sepsis from a urinary source, managed with broad-spectrum antibiotics, fluids, and vasopressor support weaning. Concurrently found to have vitamin D deficiency with 25-OH vitamin D level of 12 ng/mL; started on cholecalciferol 50,000 units weekly for eight weeks. He also has a longstanding history of migraine with aura, currently stable on prophylaxis; no headaches during admission. Plan: complete antibiotic course, repeat cultures, vitamin D repletion with level recheck, and continue migraine regimen at discharge.

ED visit: 19-year-old male presents after right upper quadrant pain for two days, postprandial, with nausea; ultrasound demonstrates gallstones without wall thickening or ductal dilation, consistent with cholelithiasis; surgery consulted, elective outpatient cholecysteectomy discussed, discharged with analgesia and dietary advice. He also describes sudden onset of exquisite right first metatarsophalangeal pain and swelling over 24 hours; joint aspirate pending clinically, monoarticular, erythematous, exquisitely tender — treated as acute gout flare with naproxen, urate level ordered for follow-up. Psychiatric history of post-traumatic stress disorder following assault last year, on sertraline, with nightmares and avoidance ongoing; refilled medication and encouraged continued trauma therapy. Exam otherwise unremarkable, afebrile. Follow-up: surgery clinic, primary care for urate and PTSD management.

Dermatology clinic. 38-year-old male with several-month history of pruritic, erythematous, scaly patches on the flexor surfaces of both elbows and behind the knees, with dry skin and lichenification from scratching. Distribution and chronic relapsing course consistent with atopic dermatitis. No known contact irritants; no lesions suggesting psoriasis or fungal infection, KOH negative. Prescribed mid-potency topical corticosteroid ointment twice daily for two weeks, liberal emollient use, fragrance-free cleansers, and brief bleach bath instructions. Reviewed triggers and avoidance of hot showers. Plan: follow-up in six weeks; if refractory, consider topical calcineurin inhibitor or referral for phototherapy.

Clinic visit. 49-year-old male presents with three weeks of productive cough, low-grade fever, and worsening fatigue. He reports dark stools occasionally and heavy coffee intake; diet poor in red meat. Exam: conjunctival pallor, scattered rhonchi with occasional wheeze, no focal consolidation. Labs: hemoglobin 9.8, MCV 72, ferritin 6, low iron saturation. Chest clear of pneumonia on exam; presentation consistent with acute bronchitis. Started on guaifenesin, inhaled albuterol as needed, and ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily with vitamin C. Stool occult blood testing ordered; colonoscopy scheduled to rule out GI bleeding source. Return sooner if fever persists beyond a week or dyspnea worsens.

Rheumatology clinic, 53F with persistent symmetric polyarthritis of MCPs, wrists, and knees, morning stiffness over an hour. RF positive at high titer, anti-CCP positive, elevated inflammatory markers — seropositive rheumatoid arthritis, currently active. On methotrexate 20 mg weekly with folic acid; adding adalimumab given inadequate control. Long-standing asthma since childhood; reports increased rescue inhaler use, nocturnal symptoms — asthma suboptimally controlled; pulmonology co-management, continue budesonide-formoterol, albuterol PRN. Exam: synovial thickening of MCPs 2-4, mild wheeze on forced expiration. Plan: labs before biologic start, PFT review, 6-week follow-up.

ED encounter. 52-year-old female brought in with acute dyspnea and pleuritic chest pain. CT angiogram of chest revealed a segmental pulmonary embolism in the right lower lobe; started on heparin drip and transitioned to rivaroxaban. She reports several months of intermittent left lower quadrant abdominal pain; CT abdomen incidentally demonstrated sigmoid diverticular disease without evidence of perforation or abscess. Abdominal and pelvic pain attributed to diverticulosis; advised high-fiber diet, outpatient GI follow-up, colonoscopy consideration after anticoagulation stabilized. Hemodynamically stable, oxygen saturating 96% on room air. Discharged on rivaroxaban 15 mg BID for 21 days then 20 mg daily, with hematology follow-up in 2 weeks. Return precautions reviewed.

52-year-old female admitted via the ED. She has a longstanding diagnosis of adult ADHD, combined presentation, stable on atomoxetine. She has epilepsy with focal seizures, well controlled on levetiracetam 1000 mg BID; levels today therapeutic. She presents with three days of a rapidly spreading, painful, warm, erythematous area on the right lower leg with tender inguinal nodes and streaking proximally, consistent with cellulitis with acute lymphangitis; no abscess on ultrasound. Afebrile, WBC 13.2. Plan: continue atomoxetine and levetiracetam, IV cefazolin with marked improvement, transition to oral cephalexin, elevation, mark erythema borders, seizure precautions on the ward.

ED note: 18-year-old male with 3 days of productive cough, fever 38.6, pleuritic right-sided chest pain; chest X-ray shows a right lower lobe infiltrate — pneumonia, unspecified organism; started on empiric antibiotics. He describes chronic intermittent claudication of the left calf after walking two blocks, with diminished dorsalis pedis pulses and an ankle-brachial index of 0.7 on the left, consistent with peripheral vascular disease; vascular surgery referral placed. Also reports chronic heartburn, worse after meals and lying flat, relieved by antacids — gastro-esophageal reflux disease; omeprazole prescribed. Diffuse abdominal and pelvic pain noted during exam, tenderness without peritoneal signs, attributed to the above conditions; urinalysis unremarkable. Plan: antibiotics, reassess in 48 hours, GI and vascular follow-up.

Nephrology clinic: 85-year-old female here for follow-up of chronic kidney disease. Creatinine 2.6, eGFR 21, stable from prior visits; urine shows trace proteinuria. She reports mild fatigue and occasional nocturia; no edema, no decreased urine output. Exam: BP 138/78, no peripheral edema, lungs clear. Impression: stage 4 chronic kidney disease, slowly progressive. Plan: continue current regimen, avoid NSAIDs and nephrotoxins, review medication list, renal-friendly diet with dietitian, monitor potassium and hemoglobin, prepare for dialysis education discussion, repeat labs in 3 months or sooner if symptoms develop.

Inpatient ward note, 83F admitted after a fall. Labs notable for 25-OH vitamin D level of 11 ng/mL; started on cholecalciferol 50,000 IU weekly for 8 weeks. Abdominal ultrasound obtained for RUQ discomfort revealed multiple gallstones within a well-distended gallbladder, no wall thickening or pericholecystic fluid, common duct normal caliber — incidental cholelithiasis, currently asymptomatic, no cholecystitis.
