Pain resolved without intervention; conservative management, low-fat diet advice. Vitamin D recheck in 3 months. Discharge planned tomorrow with PCP follow-up.

Urgent care clinic. 24-year-old male with 3 days of epigastric burning pain, nausea, and melena-free stools; prior similar episodes diagnosed as gastritis and duodenitis, currently on omeprazole 20 mg daily, which he ran out of last week. He also reports left lower quadrant cramping and constipation; CT abdomen from 6 months ago showed diverticulosis of the colon, and today's exam shows mild LLQ tenderness without peritoneal signs, consistent with diverticular disease without acute inflammation. Urinalysis shows positive nitrites and leukocyte esterase with 20 WBC/hpf — a urinary tract infection — treated with nitrofurantoin. Plan: resume omeprazole, clear liquid diet advance as tolerated, finish antibiotic course, recheck urine, return for fever, vomiting, or worsening pain.

ED note. 27-year-old female presents with two weeks of progressive exertional dyspnea, orthopnea, and bilateral lower extremity edema. History of young-onset Parkinson disease, on rasagiline and carbidopa/levodopa, well controlled. In the ED, she is afebrile, HR 110, BP 96/60, SpO2 92% on room air. Exam: jugular venous distention, bibasilar crackles, S3 gallop, 2+ pitting edema to mid-shin. Chest x-ray shows pulmonary vascular congestion and cardiomegaly; BNP 1450 pg/mL; troponin mildly elevated; echocardiogram demonstrates reduced ejection fraction of 30%. Findings consistent with new-onset heart failure, likely medication-related or idiopathic; cardiology consulted. Treated with IV furosemide with good diuresis and symptom improvement. Admitted to telemetry for diuresis, initiation of guideline-directed heart failure therapy, and neurology input regarding Parkinson medications. Parkinson disease regimen continued unchanged.

Telehealth visit. 21-year-old female with two weeks of midline lower thoracic/upper lumbar back pain after lifting boxes while moving. No radiation, no numbness or weakness, no red flags. Pain worse with bending, better with rest and ibuprofen. Exam via video: full extremity strength reported, gait normal. Impression: mechanical dorsalgia, musculoskeletal strain. Plan: NSAIDs as needed, heat, gentle stretching, activity modification, follow up in 3 weeks if not improving; imaging deferred given absence of alarm features.

Primary care clinic: 71-year-old male with facial pressure over maxillary sinuses, purulent nasal discharge, and fever for one week — acute sinusitis; started amoxicillin-clavulanate and saline irrigation. He also reports months of persistent worry, muscle tension, poor sleep, and episodic attacks of palpitations, trembling, and fear of dying lasting 10-15 minutes — generalized anxiety with panic attacks. PHQ-9/GAD-7 elevated. Started sertraline 25 mg daily with titration plan, CBT referral. No depression symptoms elicited. Follow-up in 3 weeks.

86-year-old female seen in the emergency department with two days of watery, non-bloody diarrhea, cramping, and low-grade fever after a suspect potluck meal; stool studies sent, consistent with infectious gastroenteritis and colitis. She is on furosemide and lisinopril for her chronic heart failure; exam shows mild JVD and bibasilar crackles, so diuretic dose held and daily weights ordered during rehydration to avoid volume overload. Her longstanding irritable bowel syndrome with alternating constipation and bloating flares with GI illness; she is familiar with symptom-pattern exacerbations. Plan: supportive care, oral rehydration, antiemetics as needed, stool culture, cardiology follow-up for heart failure, and reassurance that IBS symptoms should settle as the acute infection resolves.

Ward note. 56-year-old female admitted yesterday with sudden onset left-sided weakness and facial droop; non-contrast head CT was negative for hemorrhage, and MRI confirmed an acute right MCA territory ischemic stroke. NIHSS score 8. She received thromboly therapy within the window and is now on aspirin, atorvastatin 80 mg, and DVT prophylaxis. Exam: left hemiparesis 3/5 in arm and leg, left facial droop, dysarthria improving. Speech, physical, and occupational therapy consulted and initiated. Swallow evaluation passed on modified diet. Plan: continue stroke unit monitoring, daily neuro checks, secondary stroke prevention education, and planning for inpatient rehabilitation.

ICU admission. 32-year-old woman admitted from the ED with fever 103.1 F, heart rate 122, blood pressure 86/50 despite 2 liters of crystalloid, confusion, and tachypnea. Source unclear after initial evaluation: urinalysis equivocal, chest x-ray without consolidation, blood cultures drawn. Lactate 4.2. She meets criteria for sepsis with hypotension requiring vasopressors; no specific organism yet identified, treated empirically as sepsis of other/unspecified source. Started on broad-spectrum vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam, continued norepinephrine drip, central line placed. Serial lactates and cultures pending. Plan: ICU monitoring, repeat imaging, de-escalate antibiotics when cultures return.

ED visit. 47-year-old female presents with two days of left calf swelling, tightness, and pain, worse with standing. Wells score 3; duplex ultrasound confirms an acute deep vein thrombosis of the left popliteal vein. Started on apixaban 10 mg twice daily, with transition to maintenance dosing and hematology follow-up; leg elevation, compression stocking once swelling improves, and return precautions for chest pain or dyspnea discussed. Of note, she has an established diagnosis of PTSD with nightmares, hypervigilance, avoidance, and flashbacks following a motor vehicle accident, currently in trauma-focused therapy and on sertraline 100 mg daily; symptoms stable and no medication changes made. She reports the ED environment is triggering; staff asked to minimize alarms and keep visits brief.

33-year-old male seen in the ED. Two days of sore throat, rhinorrhea, cough and congestion without fever, consistent with an acute upper respiratory infection, viral in etiology. He also reports intermittent left lower quadrant abdominal cramping over the past several months; CT abdomen performed for pain shows sigmoid diverticula without evidence of diverticulitis, consistent with diverticular disease of the colon. Exam: benign abdomen, soft, mild LLQ tenderness, no peritoneal signs. Plan: supportive care, fluids, rest; high-fiber diet, increase fluid intake for the diverticulosis; GI clinic referral if symptoms persist.

Cardiology clinic follow-up. 50-year-old female presents with two weeks of progressive dyspnea on exertion and bilateral lower extremity edema. She sleeps on three pillows and reports intermittent orthopnea. Exam: JVP elevated at 10 cm, bibasilar crackles, 2+ pitting edema to mid-shin, S3 gallop. Chest X-ray shows pulmonary vascular congestion and cardiomegaly. BNP 720 pg/mL. She was previously maintained on lisinopril and carvedilol; furosemide dose increased to 40 mg daily. Plan: daily weights, 2 g sodium restriction, repeat BMP in one week, echocardiogram scheduled to assess ejection fraction. Diagnosis of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction confirmed by prior echo.

Telehealth psychiatry follow-up: 84-year-old male presents with two months of low mood, anhedonia, poor sleep, and weight loss, consistent with a first major depressive episode. PHQ-9 today 18. He also reports lifelong distractibility, impulsivity, and disorganization that meet criteria for ADHD, previously untreated; ASRS positive. Renal history notable for stage 3b chronic kidney disease, creatinine 2.1, eGFR 42, on follow-up with nephrology; no dialysis. Exam limited via video; affect depressed, psychomotor slowed. Started sertraline 25 mg daily, titration planned; considering low-dose methylphenidate once renal clearance reviewed with nephrology. Continue renal diet and fluid restrictions. Follow up in 4 weeks; safety plan reviewed, no suicidal ideation endorsed.

Memory clinic consultation. 30-year-old man with early-onset cognitive decline over three years — progressive forgetfulness, disorientation in familiar places, word-finding difficulty; now requiring supervision for daily activities. Neuropsychological testing shows global impairment; MRI reveals diffuse cortical atrophy and PET amyloid imaging positive, supporting a diagnosis of early-onset Alzheimer disease in the setting of a strong family history. His wife reports loud snoring, witnessed apneic pauses, and daytime sleepiness; home sleep study shows an apnea-hypopnea index of 22, consistent with obstructive sleep apnea — CPAP initiated. Labs also reveal stable creatinine 2.1 with eGFR 34, consistent with stage 3b chronic kidney disease, monitored by nephrology. Plan: start donepezil, CPAP adherence follow-up, renal-protective care, caregiver support referral, genetic counseling discussion, safety assessment for wandering.

Endocrinology clinic. 59-year-old female with longstanding type 1 diabetes mellitus presents for routine follow-up. Reports occasional morning hypoglycemia and increased variability in glucose readings. Uses insulin glargine at night and lispro with meals via injections; considering pump therapy. She has mild numbness in both feet consistent with known disease duration. Exam: unremarkable vital signs, feet with intact skin, diminished monofilament sensation bilaterally, no ulcers. Labs: A1c 7.8%, stable creatinine, urine albumin/creatinine ratio mildly elevated at 35 mg/g. Plan: reduce evening glargine by 2 units to address nocturnal lows, refine carb counting, initiate insulin pump discussion, continue annual dilated eye exam, add statin discussion deferred to next visit, follow-up in 3 months with A1c and renal labs.

78F admitted to medicine ward from ED. Presented with 3 days of productive cough, fever 101.8, hypoxia to 88% — CXR shows right lower lobe infiltrate consistent with pneumonia, started ceftriaxone and azithromycin. Underlying heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (30% on last echo); mild bibasilar crackles, mild LE edema, continuing furosemide 40 mg daily, daily weights, strict I/O. Hospital PTSD flaring with admission — nightmares, hypervigilance, refusing sleeping pills; psychiatric consult adjusting prazosin at bedtime, supportive counseling. Liver ultrasound during admission shows diffuse hepatic steatosis; LFTs mildly elevated, consistent with fatty liver — counseled on diet, no hepatotoxins. Plan: complete antibiotic course, cardiology follow-up, psychiatry follow-up after discharge.

Pediatric pulmonology clinic, 21-year-old female for asthma follow-up. Reports nighttime awakenings twice weekly and albuterol rescue use three to four times weekly, especially with exercise and upper respiratory infections. Exam: scattered expiratory wheezes, prolonged expiratory phase, SpO2 97%. Spirometry shows FEV1 68% predicted with 14% bronchodilator response. Assessment: asthma, not optimally controlled. Plan: escalate to medium-dose inhaled corticosteroid with long-acting beta agonist, continue rescue albuterol, spacer technique reviewed, written action plan updated, allergy testing offered, follow-up in six weeks.

Hospital ward, 42-year-old male admitted with 2 weeks of exertional dyspnea, orthopnea, and leg swelling. Found to be in new-onset atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response; free T4 elevated and TSH suppressed, consistent with thyrotoxicosis as the likely precipitant. BNP 1,240; echocardiogram shows reduced EF of 30% with global hypokinesis, consistent with heart failure. Additionally noted to have cold, dusky right toes with diminished pedal pulses and diminished ankle-brachial index on the right, consistent with peripheral arterial disease of the lower extremity. Exam: JVP elevated, bibasilar crackles, 2+ pitting edema to mid-shin. Plan: methimazole, beta-blockade, IV furosemide with response monitoring, anticoagulation for AFib, vascular surgery consult for the PAD, and endocrinology follow-up.

ED then ward admission. 47-year-old male presents with 2 days of watery diarrhea, cramping, and low-grade fever after a suspect meal; stool studies sent, presumed infectious gastroenteritis, managed with IV fluids and antiemetics. PMH significant for COPD on salmeterol/fluticasone with occasional rescue inhaler use, currently stable, and osteoporosis diagnosed last year on DEXA, on calcium, vitamin D, and alendronate, without any fracture. Exam: mild diffuse abdominal tenderness without localization, lungs clear. Plan: supportive care, oral rehydration as tolerated, continue inhalers and bone regimen during admission, discharge when tolerating diet.

ED note: 42-year-old female presents with sudden-onset right-sided pleuritic chest pain and dyspnea, began two days ago after a long car ride. HR 112, SpO2 89% on room air, RR 24. Lungs clear; right calf mildly swollen with tenderness. D-dimer markedly elevated; CT pulmonary angiogram demonstrates a filling defect in the right main pulmonary artery consistent with acute pulmonary embolism. Lower extremity duplex shows associated right popliteal deep vein thrombosis. Started on IV heparin drip; will transition to apixaban. Admitted to telemetry for anticoagulation and monitoring. Plan: cardiology follow-up, repeat imaging in 3 months.

Nephrology clinic: 29-year-old female with chronic kidney disease, likely reflux nephropathy, creatinine 2.4 mg/dL, eGFR 32, proteinuria controlled on losartan. Reports recurrent left lower quadrant cramping and bloating; colonoscopy last year showed diverticular disease of the sigmoid colon without complications. No fever or change in bowel habit currently. Exam: soft abdomen, mild LLQ tenderness without rebound. Plan: continue losartan, high-fiber diet and increased fluid for diverticulosis, avoid NSAIDs, repeat renal panel and urine protein in 3 months, nephrology follow-up, GI referral if recurrent diverticulitis symptoms develop.

Hospital follow-up, internal medicine clinic. 71-year-old man with idiopathic Parkinson disease, on carbidopa/levodopa 25/100 three times daily, reports resting tremor of the right hand and gait slowing but no falls. Recently admitted for acute pulmonary embolism of the right lower lobe segmental artery; now on apixaban 5 mg twice daily, INR stable, no bleeding. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with chronic dyspnea on exertion, using tiotropium inhaler daily; spirometry last year showed fixed airflow obstruction. Long-standing irritable bowel syndrome with alternating constipation and loose stools, bloating, worse with stress, no alarm features. Exam: masked facies, bradykinesia on finger tapping, coarse bibasilar end-expiratory wheezes. Plan: continue antiparkinsonian regimen, anticoagulation, inhaler therapy; dietary fiber and antispasmodic PRN for IBS; repeat CT chest in three months.

75-year-old female on the geriatric ward. Known Parkinson disease with resting tremor, rigidity, and bradykinesia, on carbidopa-levodopa; gait shuffling with postural instability. Admitted with left calf swelling; duplex ultrasound confirms left lower extremity deep vein thrombosis, started on enoxaparin transitioning to apixaban. DEXA scan shows T-score -2.8 at the hip consistent with osteoporosis without fracture; started on calcium, vitamin D, and alendronate. Labs also revealed 25-OH vitamin D level 12 ng/mL, frank deficiency; supplementation increased to 50,000 IU weekly x8 weeks. Physical therapy for mobility and fall prevention. Plan: repeat vitamin D level, anticoagulation follow-up, neurology to optimize Parkinson regimen.

Inpatient note, ICU stepdown. 76-year-old male admitted with acute pulmonary embolism — sudden dyspnea, tachycardia, CT angiogram showing segmental clot in right lower lobe; started on heparin drip. Found to be thyrotoxic with suppressed TSH <0.01, elevated free T4, started on methimazole and propranolol; thyroid uptake study pending. Concurrent acute bronchitis with productive cough and scattered rhonchi, no pneumonia on chest imaging; guaifenesin and inhaled bronchodilator as needed. Chronic eczema flare on lower legs with excoriated erythematous plaques; hydrocortisone cream continued. Plan: transition to apixaban, endocrine consultation, repeat thyroid panel, pulmonary follow-up.

26M seen in ED for left calf pain and swelling three days after a long flight. Exam: left calf 3 cm larger than right, tenderness along deep veins, mild warmth. Duplex ultrasound shows non-compressible left popliteal vein consistent with acute deep vein thrombosis; not in saphenous distribution. Started on apixaban 5 mg BID, hematology follow-up arranged. Chronic issues reviewed: longstanding heartburn responsive to omeprazole 20 mg daily, continue GERD precautions. Eczematous patches on flexor forearms and behind knees, treated with triamcinolone 0.1% cream BID and daily emollients. Labs drawn in ED: 25-OH vitamin D level 11 ng/mL, consistent with deficiency; start cholecalciferol 2000 IU daily, recheck in 3 months. No chest pain, no dyspnea. Discharge with return precautions for PE symptoms.

Telehealth visit, 77M for asthma review. Reports wheeze and shortness of breath with exertion two to three times weekly, using albuterol more than intended; step up to medium-dose ICS-LABA discussed. No nocturnal awakening last month; peak flows 70-80% predicted — asthma partially controlled. Spirometry referral pending. Weight reviewed: BMI 30.2, in obese range; discussed diet and gentle activity, which may also ease breathing. No chest pain. Plan: fluticasone-salmeterol, spacer technique reviewed, written action plan, weight-loss support resources, follow-up in 6 weeks or sooner if worsening.

58-year-old male admitted via ED with two days of oliguria and rising creatinine (3.4 mg/dL from baseline 1.1), consistent with acute kidney injury; BUN 62. Home levothyroxine 100 mcg daily for hypothyroidism (post-thyroiditis, TSH monitored q6 months). Also carries a history of gout, last flare in the right first MTP two months ago, on allopurinol 300 mg daily; uric acid 8.9. Reports recurrent unilateral throbbing headaches with photophobia and nausea, consistent with migraines, managed with sumatriptan PRN. Exam: dry mucous membranes, no joint erythema currently, neuro nonfocal. Plan: IV fluids, hold nephrotoxic agents including NSAIDs for migraine (use triptan cautiously), continue allopurinol, monitor renal function daily, endocrinology to recheck TSH after stabilization.

35-year-old male admitted via ED with 5 days of facial pressure, purulent nasal discharge, and fever, now with oliguria and rising creatinine from 1.1 to 4.2 mg/dL over 48 hours. BUN 62. Exam: tenderness over maxillary sinuses, edema of knees with crepitus bilaterally, BMI 31. CT sinuses: acute sinusitis with air-fluid levels. Renal ultrasound without obstruction; creatinine rise attributed to acute kidney injury likely prerenal/NSAID-related given heavy ibuprofen use for knee osteoarthritis pain. Held NSAIDs and nephrotoxins, IV fluids. ENT consulted for sinusitis; started intranasal saline and steroid; antibiotics deferred pending culture. Knee OA managed with acetaminophen. Nephrology following renal function.

Cardiology clinic. 37-year-old male evaluated for intermittent palpitations and irregular heartbeat. ECG today shows irregularly irregular rhythm with absent P waves, consistent with atrial fibrillation. Episodes also documented on event monitor, including a run of atrial flutter with 2:1 conduction. No structural disease on echo. CHA2DS-VASc low. Started on metoprolol succinate for rate control and anticoagulation discussed. Avoidance of alcohol, caffeine, and stimulants advised. Holter follow-up in 2 weeks to assess rate control and arrhythmia burden.

Hospital ward progress note. 74-year-old male admitted with left leg swelling. Duplex ultrasound confirms acute deep vein thrombosis of the left popliteal vein; started on apixaban. History of coronary artery disease with prior stenting, on aspirin and atorvastatin, currently free of chest pain; ECG shows no acute ischemic change. Also has long-standing cigarette habit, about 1.5 packs daily for 45 years, FTND score 8/10; nicotine replacement patch 21 mg started during admission with quitline referral. Exam: left calf 3 cm larger than right, mild tenderness, no ulceration; heart sounds regular, lungs clear. Plan: continue apixaban 5 mg BID, complete NRT transition at discharge, cardiology follow-up in two weeks, repeat duplex in three months.

Hospital admission. 48-year-old male presents with 3 days of anuria, nausea, and confusion after an episode of severe vomiting and diarrhea. Creatinine 6.8 mg/dL (baseline 1.0), BUN 92, potassium 6.1. Impression: acute kidney failure, likely prerenal from volume depletion; received IV fluids, hyperkalemia treated with calcium gluconate and insulin/dextrose. Urine output improving after rehydration; no dialysis required at this time. Renal ultrasound unremarkable, no obstruction. Plan: strict intake/output, daily BMP, nephrology follow-up, avoid NSAIDs. Creatinine down to 3.4 by day 3; continue supportive care.

26-year-old male seen in urgent care for two weeks of lower abdominal and pelvic pain, intermittent and cramping in nature, without fever, vomiting, or bowel changes. Exam shows mild lower abdominal tenderness without rebound or guarding; urinalysis unremarkable, and no acute surgical cause identified. Workup is supportive and symptomatic management initiated. Incidentally, screening lipid panel obtained last month showed significantly elevated LDL and low HDL consistent with hyperlipidemia; he has a strong family history of early heart disease. Plan: analgesics as needed, dietary and lifestyle counseling, start rosuvastatin, repeat lipids in three months, and return for worsening or persistent pain.

88-year-old male seen in clinic for 3 days of sore throat and painful urination. Reports odynophagia, low-grade fever 99.9 F, no cough. Also dysuria, urinary frequency, and foul-smelling urine for 2 days. Exam: pharynx erythematous with exudate on tonsils, no exudation beyond pharynx; no cervical lymphadenopathy. Suprapubic tenderness, no CVA tenderness. Urinalysis: positive nitrites, leukocyte esterase, many WBCs; rapid strep negative. Plan: supportive care with warm saline gargles and analgesics for acute pharyngitis; start nitrofurantoin for urinary tract infection. Increase fluids, follow up if symptoms persist beyond 48 hours.

Sleep medicine telehealth visit. 25-year-old female with loud snoring, witnessed pauses in breathing, and daytime sleepiness (Epworth score 16). BMI unremarkable; tonsils mildly enlarged. Home sleep apnea test shows apnea-hypopnea index of 18 with oxygen desaturations to 88%, confirming obstructive sleep apnea. Plan: initiate CPAP 8 cm H2O with heated humidification, mask fitting arranged, sleep hygiene counseling, weight stable, follow up in 6 weeks with CPAP download data to assess adherence and residual events.

Internal medicine clinic. 73-year-old male presents with 2 months of unintentional 12-lb weight loss, heat intolerance, palpitations, tremor, and loose stools. Exam: heart rate 112 irregularly regular, fine hand tremor, warm moist skin, mild lid lag without proptosis, thyroid diffusely enlarged and smooth, no bruit. Labs: TSH <0.01, free T4 elevated at 3.2, consistent with thyrotoxicosis; plan to start methimazole and beta-blockade with propranolol, endocrinology referral, repeat labs in 4-6 weeks. He also describes 6 months of progressive bilateral calf pain with walking, relieved by rest, and exam reveals absent posterior tibial pulses bilaterally with an ankle-brachial index of 0.7 on the right and 0.75 on the left, consistent with peripheral vascular disease. Plan: daily aspirin, statin therapy, supervised walking program, podiatry and foot care education, vascular surgery referral for evaluation.

Internal medicine clinic, 69-year-old male veteran presenting with tremor, heat intolerance, 12-lb weight loss, and palpitations. Exam: HR 112 irregular, fine tremor, warm moist skin, thyroid diffuse and mildly enlarged without bruit. TSH <0.01, free T4 elevated, consistent with thyrotoxicosis; started on methimazole. Also has longstanding hyperlipidemia; LDL 148 on atorvastatin 20 mg, to be uptitrated once thyroid status stabilizes. He describes nightmares, hypervigilance, avoidance of crowds, and flashbacks related to combat deployment, consistent with post-traumatic stress disorder; currently managed with sertraline 100 mg and trauma-focused therapy, which will continue. Plan: repeat TFTs in 6 weeks, beta-blockade with propranolol for symptom control, lipid panel in 3 months, behavioral health follow-up maintained.

Telehealth visit. 20-year-old male (patient is male; presenting for recurrent headaches) — correction: 21-year-old male college student with episodic unilateral throbbing headaches, photophobia, nausea, and aura of flashing lights, lasting 4-6 hours, occurring about three times monthly, interfering with classes. Neurologic review and prior exam are normal; no red flags. Pattern consistent with migraine with aura. Trial of sumatriptan 50 mg at onset, headache diary, sleep hygiene counseling. Follow up in 6 weeks or sooner if frequency increases.

65-year-old male, primary care clinic. Type 1 diabetes mellitus since age 22, on insulin pump, A1c 7.4%; reports increased facial pressure, purulent nasal discharge, and fever for five days; exam shows maxillary sinus tenderness, consistent with acute sinusitis; started on amoxicillin-clavulanate for ten days and saline irrigation. He also has known diverticular disease of the sigmoid colon from prior colonoscopy, with occasional left lower quadrant cramping; currently asymptomatic, no tenderness today, advised to maintain high-fiber diet. Exam otherwise benign, foot exam with monofilament intact. Plan: continue basal-bolus insulin via pump, monitor glucose more frequently during infection, recheck in two weeks; colonoscopy surveillance per GI.

Neurology clinic. 25-year-old female evaluated for 8 months of progressive right-hand tremor at rest, slowness, smaller handwriting, and right leg dragging when walking; family noticed decreased arm swing on the right. Exam: masked facies, resting pill-rolling tremor right hand, cogwheel rigidity right arm and leg, bradykinesia on finger tapping, reduced arm swing with shuffling gait; no cerebellar or sensory deficits. Symptoms, asymmetric onset, and examination findings are consistent with young-onset Parkinson disease. Plan: initiate carbidopa-levodopa trial with titration; physical therapy and exercise program; genetic counseling discussion given young age; MRI brain to exclude mimics; follow-up in 6 weeks to assess medication response and side effects.

Telehealth endocrinology follow-up. 65-year-old female seen for fatigue, cold intolerance, dry skin, and mild constipation over the past several months. Post-treatment status following radioactive iodine therapy for Graves disease years ago; now biochemically hypothyroid. TSH elevated at 12.4 mIU/L, free T4 low at 0.6 ng/dL. Currently on levothyroxine 75 mcg daily; dose will be increased to 100 mcg daily. No goiter or neck complaints. Recheck TSH and free T4 in 8 weeks. Advised to take thyroid hormone on empty stomach. Symptoms expected to improve with dose optimization.

Urgent care visit. 60-year-old male with three days of myalgias, low-grade fever, sore throat, and nasal congestion — exam consistent with a viral syndrome; negative rapid strep and influenza swab. Advised supportive care, fluids, rest, and acetaminophen. Additionally, he has a chronic pruritic, dry, erythematous rash in flexural areas with lichenification, consistent with his longstanding eczema; recently flared. Prescribed triamcinolone 0.1% ointment twice daily for two weeks, continuation of fragrance-free emollients, and avoidance of hot showers. No antibiotic indicated for the viral illness. Return if fever exceeds 101, symptoms worsen after ten days, or rash shows signs of infection.

Clinic visit, 21-year-old woman referred for elevated blood pressure readings on three separate occasions, today 152/96; diagnosis of essential primary hypertension established after secondary workup was unremarkable. Ultrasound obtained for mild RUQ fullness demonstrates hepatic steatosis consistent with fatty liver disease; LFTs mildly elevated. She also reports diffuse muscle aches and bilateral leg pain after starting a gym program, exam shows tenderness of thigh and calf muscles without swelling, consistent with myalgia and limb pain from soft tissue strain. Plan: begin lisinopril 10 mg daily, dietary counseling, gradual return to activity, NSAIDs PRN for muscle pain, repeat labs and BP check in four weeks.

Pulmonary clinic visit. 80-year-old woman brought in by her daughter. Alzheimer disease, moderate stage, on donepezil 10 mg daily; MMSE 16/30 earlier this year, gradually increasing forgetfulness and needs help with dressing. Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with chronic productive cough and dyspnea on exertion, on salmeterol/fluticasone inhaler; spirometry shows non-reversible obstruction. Additionally carries asthma with episodic nocturnal wheeze and marked reversibility on prior testing; albuterol rescue used twice weekly, currently overusing it. Exam: thin, pleasant, forgetful; expiratory wheezing bilaterally, prolonged expiration. Plan: reinforce inhaler technique with caregiver, add leukotriene modifier for asthma control, continue maintenance inhaler, pneumococcal and influenza vaccination, cognitive reassessment at next neurology visit.

Primary care clinic. 32-year-old female here for follow-up of elevated blood pressure; today's reading 152/96, with home log averaging 148/92, confirming essential hypertension. Started on lisinopril 10 mg daily with sodium reduction and home BP monitoring. She also reports occasional calf cramping with walking and cold hands; pulses intact but ankle-brachial index mildly reduced bilaterally, suggesting early peripheral vascular disease; will begin supervised walking program and check lipids. Labs drawn previously show ALT mildly elevated with hepatic ultrasound revealing diffuse echogenic liver consistent with fatty liver disease; no viral hepatitis on serologies. Plan: repeat metabolic panel in four weeks, continue weight-neutral dietary counseling, abstain from alcohol, and follow up in six weeks to reassess blood pressure and liver enzymes.

Hospital ward progress note: 81-year-old male admitted after fall at home. History significant for alcohol use disorder with daily heavy drinking, withdrawal risk monitored with CIWA scoring, thiamine and folate given, lorazepam PRN; patient reports prior unsuccessful quit attempts and agrees to detox referral. Bilateral knee pain with crepitus on exam, medial joint line tenderness, standing films show joint space narrowing and osteophytes consistent with osteoarthritis of the knees; managed with acetaminophen and topical diclofenac, PT consult. Plan: continue withdrawal protocol, addiction medicine consultation, mobility assessment, orthopedic follow-up for knee OA, home safety evaluation.

Clinic follow-up: 54-year-old male with long-standing seizure disorder, on levetiracetam 500 mg BID, reports one generalized tonic-clonic seizure last week after missed doses. Also complains of sore throat, nasal congestion, and cough for three days, consistent with an upper respiratory infection. Epigastric burning and nausea for two weeks; prior endoscopy showed gastritis and duodenitis, currently taking omeprazole. Creatinine 2.1 mg/dL, eGFR 38, consistent with his stage 3b chronic kidney disease. Plan: resume antiepileptic adherence, check levetiracetam level, supportive care for URI, continue PPI, avoid NSAIDs, nephrology follow-up, repeat renal panel in 4 weeks.

Psychiatry clinic, new patient. 32-year-old female presenting with lifelong difficulty focusing, chronic disorganization, losing items, missing deadlines, and restlessness that impair her work as a graphic designer. Childhood symptoms confirmed with school reports. ASRS-v1.1 strongly positive; assessment consistent with attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, combined presentation. No mood, anxiety, or substance concerns; exam otherwise unremarkable. Plan: start on atomoxetine 40 mg daily titrating to 80 mg, coaching on organization strategies, follow-up in four weeks to assess response and tolerability.

Urgent care clinic, 30-year-old male with two weeks of palpitations, heat intolerance, tremor, and unintentional 6-lb weight loss. Exam: fine tremor, mild diffuse thyromegaly, HR 112 regular. Labs: TSH <0.01, free T4 elevated — thyrotoxicosis; started on methimazole, endocrinology referral. He also reports bilateral knee pain worse with stairs and after activity, crepitus on exam, tibiofemoral tenderness without effusion — osteoarthritis of the knees; NSAIDs avoided pending workup, acetaminophen and quadriceps strengthening advised. Urinalysis shows pyuria and positive nitrites with dysuria; UTI treated with nitrofurantoin course. Follow-up in two weeks with repeat labs.

Hospital admission note, 82-year-old man brought from home with 3 days of profuse watery diarrhea, vomiting, and fever; stool culture pending, clinically infectious gastroenteritis and colitis, likely foodborne. History of alcohol related disorders — chronic heavy alcohol use with prior withdrawal admissions; currently on thiamine and folate, CIWA monitoring given withdrawal risk. He reports diffuse muscle aches and bilateral limb pain without focal weakness, attributed to myalgia and soft tissue pain from dehydration and immobility. Labs: creatinine 3.4 from baseline 1.1, BUN 62, consistent with acute kidney injury/acute renal failure, presumed prerenal; urine output 15 mL/hr. Plan: IV fluids, antiemetics, thiamine continued, hold nephrotoxins, monitor electrolytes and renal function q12h, GI isolation precautions, symptom-triggered withdrawal protocol, nephrology consulted.

56F outpatient internal medicine visit. Incidentally elevated transaminases found on routine labs: ALT 74, AST 58. Hepatitis B and C serologies negative, ferritin normal, ANA negative, alcohol use rare. Right upper quadrant ultrasound demonstrates diffuse increased echogenicity of the liver parenchyma with posterior attenuation, findings consistent with fatty liver disease (hepatic steatosis). Exam benign, no hepatomegaly or stigmata of chronic liver disease. Plan: lifestyle counseling with low-carbohydrate diet and 150 min/week aerobic activity, weight reduction goal of 5-7%, repeat hepatic panel in 12 weeks, consider Fibro-4 score to assess for fibrosis. Referred to nutrition. No right upper quadrant pain reported.

Internal medicine clinic. 60-year-old male for follow-up of cholesterol and bone health. Fasting lipid panel: total cholesterol 248, LDL 172, HDG 38, triglycerides 190 — mixed hyperlipidemia, inadequately controlled on atorvastatin 20 mg; dose increased to 40 mg nightly. DEXA scan last month showed T-score -2.7 at the lumbar spine and -2.5 at the femoral neck, consistent with osteoporosis without any fracture. No falls or fractures reported. Started calcium 1000 mg and vitamin D 1000 IU daily; discussed bisphosphonate therapy, alendronate 70 mg weekly initiated. Repeat lipid panel and bone density in 12 months. Weight-bearing exercise encouraged.

Telehealth follow-up. 20-year-old woman with alcohol use disorder, drinking daily up to a fifth of spirits, previously engaged in a brief intervention and now enrolled in an alcohol treatment program; reports craving is better on naltrexone. She has a documented history of osteoporosis on DEXA with T-score of -2.7 at the lumbar spine, without any history of fragility or pathologic fracture; on calcium, vitamin D, and alendronate. Also carries a diagnosis of chronic kidney disease, stage 3, creatinine 1.6, eGFR 45, under nephrology follow-up. Plan: continue alcohol counseling and naltrexone, monitor liver panel, repeat DEXA in 2 years, fall-prevention counseling, renal panel in 3 months, and maintain abstinence goals.

Hospital ward admission. 84-year-old male admitted with three days of left first metatarsophalangeal joint swelling, redness, and exquisite pain, classic for gout; serum uric acid 8.9. Started colchicine with improvement. Concurrent complaints of facial pressure, purulent nasal discharge, and fever — exam shows sinus tenderness with mucopurulent drainage, diagnosed as acute sinusitis, treated with cefuroxime. He also reports diffuse lower abdominal and pelvic pain without localizing signs; urinalysis negative, abdomen soft with mild suprapubic tenderness, managed with analgesia and monitoring; imaging unremarkable. Podiatry and rheumatology consulted regarding long-term urate-lowering therapy. Pain improving, afebrile, anticipated discharge tomorrow with allopurinol to start after acute flare resolves.

86M brought to the ED with 90 minutes of crushing substernal chest pain radiating to the left arm, diaphoresis. ECG: ST elevation in leads II, III, aVF. Troponin I markedly elevated. Acute myocardial infarction (inferior STEMI) diagnosed; immediate transfer for primary PCI. History also includes benign prostatic hyperplasia with nocturia, weak stream, hesitancy; on tamsulosin, previously stable. Urinary catheter placed during admission without difficulty. Post-PCI plan: dual antiplatelet therapy, high-intensity statin, beta blocker, serial troponins, resume alpha-blocker, monitor for urinary retention, cardiology follow-up in 2 weeks.

18-year-old female seen in dermatology clinic for a pruritic, scaly, erythematous rash in the antecubital fossae and behind the knees, recurring since childhood, consistent with atopic dermatitis. She also reports a first episode of sudden severe pain, redness, and swelling of the right first metatarsophalangeal joint two weeks ago; joint aspiration during an urgent visit showed negatively birefringent needle-shaped crystals, confirming gout. Plan: continue triamcinolone ointment to flares and daily moisturizer for the eczema; for gout, complete naproxen course, discuss allopurinol if attacks recur, dietary counseling, follow-up in six weeks.

Primary care clinic. 22-year-old male seen for fatigue and exertional dyspnea. Labs: hemoglobin 9.8 with microcytic indices, ferritin 8, consistent with iron deficiency anemia; started ferrous sulfate 325 mg daily with vitamin C. Also found vitamin D 25-OH level of 14 ng/mL; began cholecalciferol 2000 IU daily. At two prior visits BP was 150/94 and 152/96; today 148/92, confirming essential hypertension; started lisinopril 10 mg daily and encouraged low-sodium diet and exercise. Repeat CBC and BP check in 6 weeks. Dietary review for iron sources; no GI bleeding reported.

Clinic visit. 39-year-old male presents with chronic lower extremity aching and cramping on walking, consistent with peripheral vascular insufficiency; ankle-brachial index 0.85 bilaterally, pulses diminished at dorsalis pedis. Also reports scaly, erythematous plaques over elbows and scalp, characteristic of psoriasis, managed with topical clobetasol. Chronic bilateral knee pain with crepitus and joint-space narrowing on X-ray, consistent with osteoarthritis of the knees; takes naproxen PRN. Today also complains of intermittent diffuse lower abdominal and pelvic pain without fever or GI bleeding; exam shows mild lower abdominal tenderness without peritoneal signs. Plan: continue vascular workup with duplex ultrasound, continue topical steroid and NSAIDs, analgesia and urinalysis for pelvic pain, follow-up in 4 weeks.

51M in primary care clinic for recurrent unilateral throbbing headaches with photophobia, nausea, and aura, occurring about 3 times monthly — consistent with migraine; episodic sumatriptan provides partial relief. Also under evaluation for low bone density: recent DEXA shows T-score of -2.6 at the lumbar spine, confirming osteoporosis without any current or prior fracture. No steroid use, no secondary causes identified on labs. Exam nonfocal, spine nontender. Plan: start a bisphosphonate with calcium and vitamin D supplementation, headache diary, consider prophylactic agent if frequency increases, repeat DEXA in 2 years, return sooner for red-flag headache features.

Endocrinology clinic. 55-year-old female with type 1 diabetes mellitus since age 19, on an insulin pump with continuous glucose monitoring; recent A1c 7.2%, no reported hypoglycemic episodes, mild background retinopathy screening up to date. Over the past year she developed fatigue, cold intolerance, dry skin, and modest weight gain; labs show TSH 9.6 with normal free T4, consistent with hypothyroidism, likely autoimmune given her history. Started levothyroxine 50 mcg daily, to be taken apart from meals. Exam: mild thyroid enlargement without nodularity, otherwise unremarkable. Plan: repeat TSH in 8 weeks to titrate replacement, continue current insulin regimen, annual thyroid antibody testing considered, follow-up visit in 3 months.

Telehealth visit. 82-year-old female with recurrent retrosternal burning and acid regurgitation, worse after meals and when lying flat, partially relieved by antacids — consistent with GERD. No dysphagia, weight loss, or melena. On pantoprazole 40 mg daily for 8 weeks with residual nighttime symptoms. Plan: elevate head of bed, avoid late meals, increase to BID dosing for 4 weeks; if symptoms persist, schedule EGD to exclude erosive disease or Barrett's.

ED note, 80-year-old female brought in by EMS for sudden dyspnea and right-sided pleuritic chest pain. History notable for lifelong attention-deficit hyperactivity disorder, managed with methylphenidate, with persistent inattention, restlessness, and impulsivity per family report. On arrival: HR 118, RR 26, SpO2 88% on room air. CT pulmonary angiogram shows a filling defect in the right main pulmonary artery consistent with pulmonary embolism. Troponin mildly elevated, echocardiogram shows RV strain. Started on IV heparin and admitted to telemetry. ADHD medications continued on admission; behavioral health consulted to support regimen adherence during hospitalization. Plan: transition to apixaban, monitoring of coagulation parameters, and close follow-up of her longstanding ADHD symptom management.

ICU admission note. 34-year-old male admitted with fever, tachycardia, hypotension, and altered mental status; blood cultures grew gram-positive organisms — sepsis with source being soft tissue infection at an injection site, aggressively treated with broad-spectrum antibiotics and fluids. History of severe alcohol use disorder with daily heavy drinking and withdrawal managed with benzodiazepines per CIWA protocol. DEXA scan during prior admission revealed osteoporosis with low bone mineral density, without any pathological fracture. Plan: continue sepsis bundle, taper sedation, thiamine and folate for alcohol-related disorder, alcohol counseling and rehab referral, calcium and vitamin D with bisphosphonate consideration for osteoporosis.

Telehealth visit: 87-year-old female with several weeks of unintentional weight loss, heat intolerance, palpitations, and tremor. She reports loose stools and difficulty sleeping. Exam via video notable for fine hand tremor, tachycardia at 112 bpm, and mild lid lag. Labs from last week: suppressed TSH <0.01, elevated free T4 and free T3, consistent with thyrotoxicosis. Plan: start low-dose methimazole with cardiology input given her age, repeat thyroid function tests in four weeks, counsel on symptoms of thyroid storm, and follow up by phone in one week to assess tolerance.

Urology clinic visit. 41-year-old female with longstanding obstructive voiding symptoms: weak stream, hesitancy, nocturia twice nightly, and sensation of incomplete emptying. No dysuria or fever. Post-void residual 110 mL. Cystoscopy and ultrasound demonstrate an enlarged, smoothly enlarged prostate gland with no nodularity, consistent with benign prostatic hyperplasia; PSA normal. Plan: start tamsulosin 0.4 mg nightly, voiding diary, reassess symptoms in six weeks, consider transurethral resection if refractory.

Sleep medicine clinic. 19-year-old male referred for loud snoring, witnessed apneas, unrefreshing sleep, and daytime sleepiness lasting six months; roommate reports gasping during sleep. Epworth Sleepiness Scale 16. BMI exam notable for crowded oropharynx. Home sleep apnea test showed apnea-hypopnea index of 18 with oxygen desaturations to 88 percent, diagnostic of obstructive sleep apnea. Initiated on auto-titrating CPAP with heated humidification; mask fitting completed and education provided. Sleep hygiene counseling, avoid late-evening screen use and caffeine. Follow-up in six weeks to review CPAP download and adherence data.

61F brought to ED with 2 days of profuse watery diarrhea, vomiting and fever after a church picnic; several other attendees similarly ill — stool testing positive for Salmonella, consistent with infectious gastroenteritis/colitis. Found markedly unwell: creatinine 3.1 from baseline 0.8 (acute kidney injury, prerenal plus dehydration), uric acid elevated at 11.4. Also noted first metatarsophalangeal joint swollen, red, exquisitely tender — acute gout flare, triggered by dehydration. Further labs: TSH < 0.01, free T4 elevated — thyrotoxicosis, likely underlying Graves; she reports heat intolerance, tremor, 10 lb weight loss. Admitted for IV fluids, allopurinol deferred, colchicine started for gout, endocrinology consulted; will start antithyroid therapy once infection stabilizing. NPO advancing slowly, monitoring electrolytes and renal function daily.

Clinic visit. 82-year-old male referred by his wife for loud snoring, witnessed pauses in breathing overnight, and daytime somnolence; he dozes off while reading the newspaper. Epworth score 14/24. Exam: crowded oropharynx, large uvula, BMI unremarkable, lungs clear. Overnight polysomnography performed in the sleep lab showed apnea-hypopnea index of 22/hr with desaturations, consistent with obstructive sleep apnea. Plan: initiate CPAP at 8 cm H2O with heated humidification, sleep hygiene counseling, follow-up in 6 weeks with CPAP download to assess adherence and residual events.

Hospital admission, 79-year-old woman with COPD on tiotropium and fluticasone/salmeterol who also carries a diagnosis of asthma with repeated albuterol nebulizer needs, admitted with increased dyspnea and productive cough, treated with steroids and nebulizers. On hospital day three she developed RLQ pain, anorexia, and fever; CT shows acute appendicitis; surgery consulted and appendectomy planned despite elevated operative risk. Psychiatric history of PTSD from wartime trauma with nightmares and hypervigilance, decompensated in hospital; sertraline and prazosin continued, psychology consulted. Plan: continue COPD/asthma regimen postoperatively, incentive spirometry, trauma-informed care measures, and pulmonary follow-up at discharge.

Neurology clinic. 59-year-old man evaluated for progressive slowness, resting tremor of the right hand, and stooped gait over the past year; exam shows bradykinesia, cogwheel rigidity, and reduced arm swing — clinical picture consistent with Parkinson disease. Started on carbidopa-levodopa with good response. He also endorses pervasive low mood, anhedonia, poor sleep, and loss of appetite for the past several months, consistent with a major depressive episode; PHQ-9 score 18. Additionally reports recurrent left lower quadrant cramping and changes in bowel habit; CT colonography demonstrated multiple diverticula in the sigmoid colon without acute inflammation — diverticular disease. Advised high-fiber diet and hydration. Exam: masked facies, tremor at rest, no abdominal tenderness today. Plan: titrate levodopa, start sertraline and arrange counseling, add psyllium, refer to physical therapy, follow-up in six weeks.

Inpatient internal medicine note. 38-year-old male with early-onset Alzheimer disease (diagnosed two years ago, on memantine) admitted with fever, productive cough, and hypoxia; chest x-ray shows left lower lobe consolidation, treated as community-acquired pneumonia with organism unidentified, on ceftriaxone and azithromycin. He also carries a history of heart failure with reduced ejection fraction, on furosemide and lisinopril; daily weights stable, lungs with bibasilar crackles attributed to both his heart failure and pneumonia. Chronic bilateral knee osteoarthritis managed with acetaminophen and scheduled NSAIDs held during admission. Exam: oriented to person only, which is his cognitive baseline. Plan: continue antibiotics, diuresis monitoring, gentle mobilization for arthritic knees, dementia-friendly care with family at bedside, and repeat imaging before discharge.

Hospital ward admission. 78-year-old male admitted from ED with 3 days of spreading redness, warmth, and swelling of the left lower leg with a tender red streak tracking up the medial calf, consistent with cellulitis with acute lymphangitis. On arrival he was febrile to 38.9, tachycardic 118, hypotensive 88/50, confused, lactate 4.2 and WBC 18.4 — sepsis secondary to the soft tissue infection. Blood cultures drawn; broad-spectrum antibiotics started after fluid resuscitation. Plan: continue empiric vancomycin and piperacillin-tazobactam, reassess cultures at 48 hours, elevate leg, monitor for abscess requiring drainage.

84-year-old male brought to the ED by family. Found lethargic at home with poor oral intake for three days; creatinine 4.1 (baseline 1.3), BUN 78, consistent with acute kidney failure, likely prerenal; urine output 15 mL/hr. Home medications include tamsulosin 0.4 mg daily for benign prostatic hyperplasia with hesitancy and nocturia; bladder scan shows no significant retention. He also describes lifelong recurrent unilateral pulsatile headaches with light sensitivity, consistent with migraines, historically responsive to sumatriptan; NSAIDs held given renal function. Exam: dry mucous membranes, supple abdomen, enlarged prostate by prior records, no focal deficits. Plan: IV fluid resuscitation, strict intake/output, monitor electrolytes, avoid nephrotoxins, urology follow-up for BPH symptoms after renal recovery, neurology referral if headaches recur.

Inpatient ward progress note. 78-year-old male admitted with chest pain; cath showed multivessel coronary artery disease, managed medically with aspirin, atorvastatin, metoprolol, and nitroglycerin as needed for his chronic ischemic heart disease. Creatinine 2.1, eGFR 27, consistent with chronic kidney disease stage 4; nephrology following, medications renally dosed. He also carries a diagnosis of PTSD from military service, with nightmares and startle response noted during admission; psychiatric consultation adjusted his prazosin and continued sertraline. Reports recurrent epigastric and pelvic abdominal pain; CT abdomen unremarkable for obstruction or mass, pain managed conservatively, outpatient GI scheduled. Afebrile, hemodynamically stable. Awaiting discharge planning with home health.

Primary care clinic. 73-year-old female seen for management of essential hypertension and chronic back pain. Home BP log averages 158/92 on amlodipine 5 mg daily. She reports persistent dull, aching dorsalgia across the lower and mid back, worse with prolonged standing, without radiculopathy, bowel or bladder changes, or trauma. Exam: BP 156/90, heart regular without murmur, no edema, spine with paravertebral muscular tenderness and mild lumbar stiffness, normal neuro exam of lower extremities, negative straight leg raise. Plan: increase amlodipine to 10 mg daily, add lisinopril, encourage low-sodium diet and home BP monitoring; back pain managed with heat, stretching, scheduled NSAIDs, and physical therapy referral; no imaging indicated at this time given absence of red flags; follow-up in 4 weeks.

Hospital admission, 26M with 4 days of fever, productive cough, and dyspnea. CXR: right lower lobe infiltrate — community-acquired pneumonia, organism unspecified; started on ceftriaxone and azithromycin. Admission labs also show creatinine 2.6 mg/dL from baseline 1.0 with reduced urine output, BUN 42 — acute kidney injury presumed prerenal/injury mixed; nephrology consulted, IV fluids, holding nephrotoxins, monitoring input/output. Hemoglobin 9.1 with low MCV-normal indices, unspecified anemia; iron studies pending. Smokes 1 pack/day — nicotine dependence; offered nicotine replacement patch while admitted. Interval: afebrile overnight, saturating 95% on room air.

Urgent care visit. 82-year-old male presents with 4 days of productive cough with clear sputum, low-grade fever, and chest tightness. Exam: scattered rhonchi, no wheeze, no focal consolidation; chest X-ray clear. Diagnosed with acute bronchitis — supportive care, guaifenesin, rest, return if fever persists. Also documented BMI 29.4 — overweight; discussed diet and gentle walking program given his age, nutrition handout provided.

Dermatology clinic. 24-year-old male with recurrent itchy, dry rash in flexural areas of both antecubital fossae and behind the ears, flaring for several weeks. Exam: erythematous, lichenified patches with excoriations, consistent with chronic eczema. No weeping or secondary infection. Prescribed triamcinolone 0.1% ointment twice daily for two weeks, liberal fragrance-free emollients, and oral antihistamine for itch. Advised to avoid hot showers and harsh soaps. Plan: follow up in 6 weeks; if refractory, consider topical calcineurin inhibitor.

Hospital ward admission. 64-year-old female admitted with 4 days of rapidly spreading erythema, warmth, and tenderness of the right calf with proximal lymphangitic streaking and tender inguinal lymphadenopathy, consistent with cellulitis with acute lymphangitis; started on IV cefazolin with marked improvement, afebrile 24 hours, plan to transition to oral cephalexin and discharge tomorrow. She has a long history of alcohol related disorders with prior withdrawal admissions; currently on CIWA monitoring, received lorazepam protocol, and has agreed to engage with the addiction medicine team — naltrexone planned at discharge along with detox referral. She also reports urinary frequency, weak stream, nocturia x2, and incomplete emptying; benign prostatic hyperplasia confirmed on prior ultrasound, started on tamsulosin while inpatient. Follow-up arranged with PCP in 1 week.

Clinic note. 78-year-old female here for follow-up of asthma and gout. Reports intermittent wheezing and nighttime cough; using albuterol inhaler 3-4 times weekly. No recent flares requiring steroids. Also describes a painful, swollen right first MTP joint two weeks ago, resolved with colchicine. Exam: scattered expiratory wheezes, pulse 88, no respiratory distress. Right great toe without active inflammation. Labs: uric acid 8.2 mg/dL. Plan: continue colchicine 0.6 mg daily prophylaxis, add low-dose inhaled corticosteroid for asthma control, review trigger avoidance, allopurinol initiation deferred until asthma stable. Follow-up in 6 weeks with spirometry.

Telehealth psychiatry visit. 68-year-old female with post-traumatic stress disorder after a home invasion two years ago. Continues nightmares, flashbacks, hypervigilance, avoidance of crowds, exaggerated startle; PCL-5 elevated. Also has epilepsy with recurrent focal seizures, roughly monthly, on levetiracetam 1000 mg BID; last seizure three weeks ago, no status. Exam limited via video; oriented, no postictal features. Plan: continue sertraline 100 mg and prazosin at bedtime for nightmares; continue levetiracetam, check level and EEG if seizures increase; trauma-focused therapy referral; follow up in 4 weeks.

Primary care clinic. 77-year-old male here for follow-up of hyperlipidemia; fasting lipid panel shows elevated LDL and triglycerides despite diet efforts, so atorvastatin 20 mg daily is initiated with repeat panel in three months. He also reports recurrent left lower quadrant discomfort over the past several months; CT colonography performed last month demonstrated multiple diverticula of the sigmoid colon without acute inflammation, consistent with diverticular disease of intestine. Abdominal exam is soft, mild tenderness in the left lower quadrant, no guarding. Plan: high-fiber diet, increased fluid intake, avoid nuts/seeds per patient preference, statin therapy, and return sooner for fever, severe pain, or rectal bleeding.

Infectious disease consult, inpatient. 71-year-old male admitted with three days of expanding redness, warmth, and swelling of the left lower leg with tender streaking up the medial calf, consistent with cellulitis with acute lymphangitis; no abscess on ultrasound. Marked on skin for border tracking. Known atrial fibrillation and flutter on home apixaban, ECG on admission shows irregularly irregular rhythm with flutter waves, rate 88, anticoagulation continued. Started on IV cefazolin with improving erythema; may step down to oral cephalexin. Afebrile for 24 hours. Leg elevated, serial border measurements documented. Plan: complete antibiotic course, cardiology follow-up for rhythm management, TTE previously showed preserved function.

Dermatology/rheum combined visit: 28-year-old male with chronic pruritic, erythematous, scaly patches on flexor wrists and antecubital fossae — atopic eczema; topical tacrolimus and emollients prescribed. Also has symmetric morning stiffness of MCP and wrist joints lasting over an hour, synovitis on exam, RF and anti-CCP positive — rheumatoid arthritis; started methotrexate 15 mg weekly with folic acid. Reports persistent excessive worry and restlessness for a year, with recurrent panic episodes; diagnosed generalized anxiety disorder with panic attacks, started sertraline. Labs ordered; rheum and derm follow-up in 6 weeks.

Outpatient clinic, SOAP. Subjective: 67-year-old male here for diabetes management; reports occasional polyuria and morning fatigue, adherent to metformin 1000 mg BID. Objective: fasting glucose 148, HbA1c 8.1%, BMI 27, monofilament exam normal, no retinopathy on fundoscopic exam. Assessment: type 2 diabetes mellitus, suboptimally controlled. Plan: add glipizide 5 mg daily, nutrition referral, increase activity, repeat HbA1c in 3 months, annual foot and eye exam scheduled.

Primary care clinic: 55-year-old female here for several concerns. She has type 2 diabetes mellitus, on metformin 1000 mg twice daily; A1c today 7.4%, continuing current regimen with nutrition reinforcement. For the past four days she has had sore throat, nasal congestion, and dry cough without fever, exam benign — acute upper respiratory infection, treated symptomatically. She also reports several weeks of midline low back pain without radicularity, worse with prolonged standing, exam showing paravertebral tenderness and full range of motion, negative straight leg raise; dorsalgia attributed to muscular strain, started on NSAIDs, heat, and physical therapy referral. Plan: repeat A1c in 3 months, return if back pain persists beyond 6 weeks.

Pulmonary clinic, 48-year-old male with chronic productive cough and exertional dyspnea for 2 years. Spirometry: FEV1/FVC 0.58, FEV1 62% predicted, minimal reversibility. Exam: decreased breath sounds, prolonged expiration, barrel chest. Imaging shows hyperinflation without other pathology. Diagnosed with COPD; started on tiotropium daily and albuterol as needed, pulmonary rehab referral, and annual vaccinations discussed. Inhaler technique reviewed. Pneumonia and exacerbation prevention discussed. Follow-up spirometry in 3 months.

46-year-old female seen in GI clinic for a three-month history of postprandial burning retrosternal discomfort and acid regurgitation, worse with recumbency and coffee, partially relieved by antacids. She denies dysphagia, weight loss or melena. Exam: comfortable, abdomen soft, non-tender, no masses. Clinical diagnosis of gastro-esophageal reflux disease. Plan: pantoprazole 40 mg daily for eight weeks, avoid late meals, elevate head of bed, limit caffeine and alcohol; alarm symptom education; reassess symptoms at follow-up visit.

Outpatient clinic, SOAP format. S: 23-year-old female with months of excessive worry, difficulty concentrating, muscle tension, and episodes of palpitations, trembling, and fear of dying lasting 10-20 minutes, occurring several times monthly. Also reports unilateral throbbing headaches with photophobia and nausea, roughly twice monthly, improved with rest. O: Alert, no distress at rest, normal neurologic exam, vital signs stable. A: Generalized anxiety disorder with panic attacks; migraine without aura. P: Started escitalopram 10 mg daily, CBT referral, headache diary; sumatriptan 50 mg PRN at migraine onset. Avoid triggers, sleep hygiene. Follow up six weeks.

28-year-old female presenting to family practice telehealth visit. She has fatigue, cold intolerance, dry skin and weight gain over six months. TSH elevated at 9.8 with low free T4, consistent with hypothyroidism, likely Hashimoto's given positive anti-TPO antibodies; started on levothyroxine 75 mcg daily. BMI 27.4, counseled on diet and exercise for overweight status. She also reports chronic heartburn, worse after meals and when lying down, with regurgitation; exam unremarkable; clinically GERD. Plan: omeprazole 20 mg daily, lifestyle modification, repeat TSH in eight weeks.

30F seen in primary care clinic. Lipid panel: total cholesterol 248, LDL 172, triglycerides 180, HDL 42 — consistent with hyperlipidemia; ASCVD risk low at her age; advised therapeutic lifestyle changes, repeat panel in 3 months, consider statin if LDL remains elevated. Reports drinking 6-8 beers nightly for the past 2 years, several failed attempts to cut down, morning shakes relieved by drinking — meets criteria for alcohol use disorder, moderate severity. CAGE positive 4/4. Referred to addiction medicine, started naltrexone 50 mg daily after negative pregnancy test, thiamine supplementation, encouragement to attend AA. LFTs mildly elevated, GGT 120. Mental health screening negative for depression. Follow-up in 4 weeks with repeat labs.

Hospital ward admission: 48-year-old male admitted with fever, productive cough, and hypoxia; chest x-ray shows right lower lobe consolidation, treated as community-acquired pneumonia with ceftriaxone and azithromycin, organism not yet identified. History includes idiopathic Parkinson disease (Hoehn-Yahr stage 2, tremor and bradykinesia, on carbidopa/levodopa) and paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on apixaban, rate-controlled with metoprolol. He also carries a longstanding ADHD diagnosis, managed with atomoxetine, which he continues during admission. Exam: coarse crackles right base, irregularly irregular pulse, resting tremor left hand. Plan: complete antibiotics, repeat imaging, continue Parkinson medications on schedule to avoid deterioration, monitor rhythm, and resume outpatient neurology and psychiatry follow-up at discharge.
